384YE Autumn Equinox Conclave sessions.d: Precedence went to the Rod and Shield. Vas Radovanovna Esskivik became Gloaming Sentinel, Aleksander Zoravih Novosad Arcane Architect, Æsa Sigeling Imperial Magus and Ibiss Netherwatch Archmage of Spring. Dawn accepted Tharim's bargain, giving up mana and farm income for a year in return for 1000 knights. The Heralds of Tharim were invited to the Hall of Worlds. Rosalynne de Gauvain and Sidlore Edric Charge de Gauvain were declared sorcerers for provoking Hayaak, but Solene d'Alba was not. Attempts to condemn or interdict Thunderous Deluge failed, while a statement that Conclave had endorsed its casting passed. Support for persecuted Suranni magicians passed, and Eyes of the Soul's Past was shared with the Axou.

n.Dawn: Through the Black Frost concord, Dawn's mages and farmers accepted Tharim's bargain: for a year their sites yield one less mana crystal and their farms 36 fewer rings, in exchange for 1000 knights to aid them in the Barrens.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but the Barrens they hold are where Tharim's knights, bargained for by Dawn, are meant to give assistance.

t.The Barrens: The bargain Dawn struck with Tharim concerned his offer of assistance in the Druj-held Barrens, bringing 1000 of the Bound King's knights to the fight there.

384YE Autumn Equinox Imperial elections.d: Senators were elected for Casinea, Hahnmark, Kahraman, Morrow, Semmerholm, Skarsind, Tassato, Therunin, Upwold, Volodmartz and Zenith. The Senate appointed generals for seven armies, two Advisors on Orc Affairs, the Imperial Administrator, the Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves and others. The Synod chose Cardinals of Loyalty and Pride, two inquisitors, several champions and other religious titles, with vote counts recorded. The Military Council filled posts including Quartermaster General and Imperial Warcaster. The Conclave elected three Grandmasters, and candidates declared for titles such as Imperial Magus. The Bourse auctioned seats including the Great Pits of Ennerlund for 486 thrones and voted on others.

n.Dawn: Zadkiel de Coeurdefer was elected Senator for Semmerholm, the Dawnish-held territory.
n.Druj: Cadeus was named Senator for Zenith, a territory then held by the Druj.
n.Highguard: Solomon was elected Senator for Casinea, the Highborn-held territory.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Rasp was elected Senator for Skarsind. Stormcrow Skred and Atla were each appointed Advisor on Orc Affairs.
n.Navarr: Travid Longest Path was elected Senator for Therunin, the Navarr-held territory.
n.The Brass Coast: Delara i Fijadoz i Guerra was elected Senator for Kahraman, the Brass Coast territory.
n.The League: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato was elected Senator for Tassato, the League-held territory.
n.The Marches: Matilda Reaper was elected Senator for Upwold, the Marcher-held territory.
n.Urizen: Juliana was elected Senator for Morrow, the Urizen-held territory.
n.Varushka: Desilav Sergeyevich Jesen was elected Senator for Volodmartz, the Varushkan-held territory.
n.Wintermark: Hengest Dun was elected Senator for Hahnmark, the Wintermark-held territory.

t.Casinea: Solomon was elected as Casinea's senator.
t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun was elected as Hahnmark's senator.
t.Kahraman: Delara i Fijadoz i Guerra was elected as Kahraman's senator.
t.Morrow: Juliana was elected as Morrow's senator.
t.Semmerholm: Zadkiel de Coeurdefer was elected as Semmerholm's senator.
t.Skarsind: Bloodcrow Rasp was elected as Skarsind's senator.
t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato was elected as Tassato's senator.
t.Therunin: Travid Longest Path was elected as Therunin's senator.
t.Upwold: Matilda Reaper was elected as Upwold's senator.
t.Volodmartz: Desilav Sergeyevich Jesen was elected as Volodmartz's senator.
t.Zenith: Cadeus was listed as Senator for Zenith, though the territory was then held by the Druj.

384YE Autumn Equinox Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 1702 thrones and 2 crowns. The Senate gave Zenith to Urizen and ordered an appraisal of stabilising it. It created an Ambassador to the Grendel and funded the Grendel Embassy, and created a Synod Judgement of Virtuous Challenge. Disbursements funded the Burning Falcons, military resupply and the Imperial Seer's scrying. Commissions included the Black Canal, Boar's Market, the expanded Library of Hacynian, the Swords of Nearweald and improvements at Syrene's Wisdom. Several sinecures went to further scrutiny for missing details. Thornsong House failed. Title-holders announced a spy network west of Skallahn, a port at Bittershore and Giritane's Gaze.

n.Dawn: Weirwater's senator secured 50 thrones to build the Boar's Market in Astolat, letting Dawn buy bourse resources. Giritane's Gaze was announced for Weirwater, while the Laroc tourney grounds motion was withdrawn.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but Zenith, listed as held by them, was assigned by the Senate to Urizen.
n.Grendel: The Senate created an Ambassador to the Grendel, taking ambassadorial powers from the Imperial Fleet Master, and disbursed 200 thrones to pay for the completed Grendel Embassy.
n.Highguard: Highborn senators won 40 thrones for the Imperial Seer's scrying and 100 thrones to modernise the pumps of Syrene's Wisdom. Necropolis's call to appraise foreign pilgrims of the Way failed.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: a motion to abrogate the Advisor on Orc Affairs was withdrawn, and Skarsind's senator seconded the Captain of the Senate Guard appointment.
n.Jotun: The Imperial Spymaster announced a spy network west of Skallahn to supercharge the offensive against the Jotun. Researchers into Bregasland's sinking were warned of the danger from Jotun.
n.Navarr: Navarr won 250 thrones to expand the Library of Hacynian into a great library of vallorn lore, and 500 thrones for resupply went to Miaren. Thornsong House failed, and Arthur Bannerman of Navarr became Captain of the Senate Guard.
n.The Brass Coast: Madruga's senator received 400 thrones to raise the Burning Falcons and Segura's senator proposed the new Ambassador to the Grendel. No Imperial Throne was elected on Kahraman's motion.
n.The League: The League gained the Chair of the Wolf, Tender of the Blood Orchard and Reapers' Repose titles, 50 thrones for Tassato's flood repairs and a planned Scholars of the Sword Academy. The Curator of the Blood Red River will now be appointed by its National Assembly.
n.The Marches: Bridget Talbot of the Marches was elected Imperial Administrator and the Black Canal was commissioned to bring prosperity to Mournwold and Mitwold. The Breadbasket went to the Marches to ease the influx of Bregasland citizens, and the Happiston sinecure awaits scrutiny.
n.Thule: Recognising the Thule's abolition of slavery and the damage of Thunderous Deluge, the Senate lifted sanctions on Otkodov and granted its orcs free trade with the Empire.
n.Urizen: Urizen was given Zenith, which can now appoint a senator, to support the Citadel Guard. The Spiral Envoy will now be chosen by Tally of the Votes, and Thalia of Netherwatch became Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves.
n.Varushka: Varushkan senators drove the ratified Faraden and Iron Confederacy treaties and the Swords of Nearweald barracks in Ossium. Kostjya announced a self-funded port, Kostjyas Respite, on the Bittershore.
n.Wintermark: The Hall of the Unbroken, a sanctuary for former slaves in East Floes, passed but is under further scrutiny. The Beacons of Kallavesa were named for Imperial guerdon.

t.Astolat: A market-fayre, the Boar's Market, is to be built at Boar's Hollow with a Reeve of the Boars Market elected by well worn path.
t.Bastion: Bastion's senator received 40 thrones so the Imperial Seer can use scrying magics. A failed motion would have looked at escalating Bastion to the challenge of Timoj.
t.Casinea: Casinea's senator received 100 thrones to modernise the pumps of Syrene's Wisdom for better ilium returns and safer miners.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark's senator proposed the Captain of the Senate Guard appointment and seconded the Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves.
t.Hercynia: The Library of Hacynian in Hercynia is to become a great library of vallorn lore and research ways to destroy the vallorn, with 250 thrones disbursed.
t.Holberg: The Holberg Guild of Engineers may expand under the new Chair of the Wolf, and a Scholars of the Sword Academy sinecure was announced for the city. Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg donated 28 thrones to the treasury.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman's senator proposed appointing an Imperial Throne, but none was elected.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Beacons of Kallavesa were named for Imperial guerdon, and its senator proposed and seconded other motions.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov's senator seconded the Judgement of Virtuous Challenge and proposed the deferred Iron Confederacy ambassador election.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's senator proposed the Faraden treaty and seconded the lifting of sanctions on the Thule.
t.Madruga: Madruga's senator received 400 thrones to raise the Burning Falcons.
t.Miaren: Miaren's senator received 500 thrones for military and magical resupply.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova's senator proposed the Iron Confederacy treaty and seconded the Faraden treaty.
t.Mitwold: The Black Canal commission aims to improve Mitwold's prosperity, and its senator proposed the passed motion to map the Sea of Snow.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow's senator proposed assigning Zenith to Urizen and seconded the Zenith appraisal.
t.Mournwold: The Black Canal is to reach Mournwold, with Mournwold orcs working alongside Marchers. A Potato Fields mana sinecure at Happiston in the Chalkdowns passed but is under scrutiny.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis's senator proposed the failed pilgrims appraisal and seconded the Tassato repairs.
t.Ossium: The Swords of Nearweald fortified barracks were commissioned in Ossium, and a self-funded port, Kostjyas Respite, was announced on the Bittershore.
t.Otkodov: Trade sanctions on Otkodov were removed and its orcs now enjoy free trade with minimal tariffs and quick access to Imperial markets.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's senator seconded the Zenith assignment and received 200 thrones for the Grendel Embassy and 150 for the Swords of Nearweald.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Reikos's senator proposed lifting sanctions on the Thule and seconded the Grendel Embassy funding.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's senator proposed the Chair of the Wolf, and Achille di Sarvos announced the Holberg academy.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura's senator proposed the Ambassador to the Grendel and seconded the Imperial Throne motion.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm's senator proposed the withdrawn Laroc tourney grounds motion and seconded the Reapers' Repose.
t.Sermersuaq: The Hall of the Unbroken, a mana sinecure for those who endured slavery, is to be built in East Floes, though it is under scrutiny for missing details.
t.Skallahn: Building on the successful Skallahn raid, the Imperial Spymaster announced a spy network in the territory west of Skallahn.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind's senator seconded the Captain of the Senate Guard appointment.
t.Tassato: The Senate allocated 50 thrones to repair Tassato's flood damage, sparing its businesses notable loss of income this season.
t.Temeschwar: The Reapers' Repose sinecure was commissioned in Melfort, though the civil service awaits clarification from Temeschwar's senator.
t.Therunin: The motion to build Thornsong House, a hospital college for potion research in Therunin, failed.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's senator proposed the Black Canal and seconded mapping the Sea of Snow.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Volodmartz's senator proposed free trade with the Thule and seconded the Ambassador to the Grendel.
t.Weirwater: The Master of the Koboldi announced Giritane's Gaze, a great mandowla statue supporting Weirwater's miners funded by its senator. The senator also received 50 thrones for the Boar's Market.
t.Zenith: Zenith was assigned to Urizen and can appoint a senator, and an appraisal was ordered into stabilising it and supporting returning refugees.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Secure Wunderkind Woods motion defined the status of Holmauer Park, recognising the Rebeshi Players as guardians and creating the Tender of the Blood Orchard.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Cabal Lyktan and the people of Varushka announced a self-funded port and town, Kostjyas Respite, on the Bittershore, with a Merchant Boyar of the Bittershore.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: The Senate commissioned the Swords of Nearweald, a fortified barracks in Ossium, with 150 thrones disbursed.

384YE Autumn Equinox interlude.d: The 350-throne Imperial Guerdon was shared among units supporting the Green Shield, Fire of the South, Hounds of Glory and Iron Helms. Military units and fleets could join a second raid on Skallahn under Marshal Orrick Bolholt, a Senate-legalised raid on Chalonsio organised by the Sumaah Republic, or a Red Door expedition to protect the koboldi. They could also go Into the Twisted Woods. Storms mitigated the Great Drought in Imperial territories but halved farm and business production and penalised mines. The drought persisted in territories outside the Imperial regio. Mandates affected Highborn and Dawnish units, Highborn congregations, and congregations near the Asavean buildings. Two rituals entered Imperial lore.

n.Dawn: Dawnish units gained extra rewards for supporting Dawnish, Highborn or Navarr armies in Dark Ranging, and were among the most effective at Into the Twisted Woods. They also had special advantages on the Red Door raid, and horse-lovers in Weirwater shared a strange exhilarating dream.
n.Druj: Zenith, held by the Druj, remained under the Great Drought and its herb gardens were cursed by the Feast of Want.
n.Grendel: Feroz and Spiral, both held by the Grendel, still suffered the Great Drought, with farms there taking a production penalty.
n.Highguard: Highborn characters could upgrade military units for one fewer wain of mithril. Under the Blade of the Pilgrims mandate, Highborn congregations gave up two votes and one liao each to aid any opportunity to fight the vallorn.
n.Jotun: Jotun-held Skallahn faced a second Imperial raid, while their holdings of Bregasland and Liathaven remained in the grip of the Great Drought.
n.Navarr: Navarr armies engaged in Dark Ranging could draw extra-rewarded Dawnish support, and Navarr units had special advantages on the Red Door raid.
n.The League: Holberg's farms received herbs from the Sand Fisher orcs. Congregations in Tassato and Temeschwar gained votes and liao from Rafael Barossa di Tassato's Reject False Gods mandate.
n.Urizen: Congregations in Redoubt gained extra votes and liao from the anti-idolatry mandate, and several rituals were added to Urizen lore through the Gift of Knowledge.
n.Varushka: Varushkan units were among the most effective at Into the Twisted Woods, which could become permanent for them if the Tower of the Manticore were built in Ossium. Congregations in Karsk gained the anti-idolatry bonus.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's assembly helped recognise Orrick Bolholt as Marshal of the Skallahn raid, in which its fleets avoid the outsider penalty. Its heroes could recover rune secrets for the Runegrott Runeforge if the Red Door raid reached the ancient tunnels, and Hahnmark's congregations gained the anti-idolatry bonus.

t.Bregasland: Outside the Imperial regio, Bregasland escaped the storms but its farms still took a -2 penalty from the Great Drought.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn here had become quiescent, but the territory remained under the Great Drought. Dawnish units supporting armies fighting the vallorn here earned extra rewards.
t.Feroz: Farms in Feroz still suffered a -2 production penalty from the Great Drought.
t.Hahnmark: Congregations in Hahnmark gained two votes and one liao while the Synod stood clearly against idolatry, and the territory was struck by the storms.
t.Holberg: Farms in Holberg received two random herbs each downtime through the Sand Fisher tithe.
t.Karsk: Congregations in Karsk gained two votes and one liao under the Reject False Gods mandate.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven remained in the Great Drought, with its farms taking a -2 penalty.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: building the Tower of the Manticore here would make Into the Twisted Woods permanently available to Dawn and Varushka.
t.Redoubt: Congregations in Redoubt gained two votes and one liao for as long as the Synod maintained its anti-idolatry stance.
t.Skallahn: Skallahn was the target of a second Imperial raid by military units and fleets under Marshal Orrick Bolholt, with rewards depending on its success.
t.Spiral: Farms in Spiral continued to suffer the -2 penalty of the Great Drought.
t.Tassato: Congregations in Tassato gained two votes and one liao from the mandate against the Asavean architect's buildings.
t.Temeschwar: Congregations in Temeschwar gained two votes and one liao while the Synod opposed idolatry.
t.Weirwater: Those in Weirwater with an affinity for horses dreamt of riding a galloping horse on an unknown shore on a moonless night, and woke exhilarated.
t.Zenith: Zenith's farms suffered the Great Drought, and the Feast of Want cursed its herb gardens to yield three fewer true vervain and one fewer of each other herb.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Dawnish military units supporting Dawnish, Highborn or Navarr armies engaged in Dark Ranging earned an extra crown and two random herbs.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in that of Lucius Ankarien Willstone, whose ritual Muffled Oar was added to Imperial lore.

384YE Autumn Equinox winds of fortune.d: The entries set out choices and opportunities rather than settled outcomes. These included a Temeschwar university appraisal, a remedy for cursed Holmauer Park, Prosperity proposals for Astolat, and Synod censure over Dawn's Barrens ambitions. Queen Rhianos offered aid to explore fallen Terunael, the Senate could map the Sea of Snow, and the Slave Lords of Rachensgrab's aerie was found. The Great Storm left Tassato badly damaged. The hylje gave the Mediator a means of contact, and Axou trade penalties continued to fade. Summer conjunction results were mixed. Koskinen and Oath-Heart were recovered and the Stone of Storms was claimed, but the Jotun kept the Spear of Bounty and Druj raiders escaped with an amulet and a text.

n.Dawn: Dawn's assembly faced Synod censure over its long dream of conquering the Barrens, while Astolat received Prosperity proposals and the enchantresses pursued Summer opportunities tied to the Eastern Sky. A Spring horror menacing the Dawnish armies in the Barrens was decisively defeated.
n.Druj: The Druj were trapped in Zenith by a Highborn crusade but unleashed an evil that threatened to taint the territory. Their raiders escaped with the Amulet of Truth and a magical text, while followers of Siakha lost the Stone of Storms and many of their number.
n.Grendel: A Grendel Waverider raiding party was stopped short of Cereva Hall in Segura after negotiations broke down. The port of Oran remained closed to Imperial fleets.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly faced choices over the Druj evil in Zenith after three seasons of crusading, and was invited to pool resources with Navarr against the vallorn. Rhianos' heralds also came to Highguard seeking adventurers for Terunael.
n.Imperial Orcs: Despite valiant efforts, the Imperial Orcs failed to deny the Spear of Bounty to the Jotun, but the Pilgrim's Shield Oath-Heart was recovered in Bregasland. A Tamazi delegation came to Anvil to speak with them.
n.Jotun: The Jotun kept the Spear of Bounty and gained the favour of Hayaak, but lost the hylje hostage Koskinen, and House Greywater escaped their execution squad. The raid on Skallahn opened a chance for the Empire to map the seas around Jotun lands.
n.Navarr: Iniska Ashwood's Pride mandate opened opportunities against the vallorn, including joint work with the Highborn assembly. Rhianos offered aid to explore Terunael, a kidnapped Navarr and their relic were rescued in Karsk, and the Feverwater expedition returned safely.
n.The Brass Coast: Cardinal of Wisdom Hembeneth i Guerra's call bore fruit in a proposed solution for Holmauer Park. Waveriders were kept from Cereva Hall in Segura, and the citizens of Madruga were among those affected by the storm's aftermath.
n.The League: The League faced an appraisal for a university in Temeschwar and a proposed remedy for cursed Holmauer Park in Holberg. Tassato was badly damaged by the surging waters of the Vassa.
n.Thule: The matter of a Thule warlock captured by the Jotun was resolved to the Thule's satisfaction, and they commended the Ambassador to Otkodov. Mapping of the Sea of Snow might extend towards Thule lands.
n.Urizen: The Highborn crusade sought to free the Urizen people of Zenith while a Druj evil threatened to taint the territory, and the Conclave discussed new rituals in Urizen lore. Druj escaped with the Amulet of Truth from Golden Cascade.
n.Varushka: The robber-boyar of Isember was executed in Karsk, a dark spirit there was allowed to flee, and the Druj destroyed two of Ossium's Bone Hives. Varushkan residents of Karsk, Karov and Ossium were among those affected by the storm's aftermath, and trouble involving the Mir Mozga was reported.
n.Wintermark: The hylje gave the Mediator of Hyljehal, Raal Dunn, a way to contact them after Koskinen's rescue. The ghosts of Turelva in Hahnmark were laid to rest, and Wintermark fleet captains were invited to help map the Sea of Snow.

t.Astolat: Pilgrims of Prosperity drew up proposals with the yeofolk to build on the growing trade brought to Astolat's fayres by the Blood Red Roads.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: its earlier successful mapping was cited as a precedent for mapping the Sea of Snow.
t.Bregasland: Dillion Fisher was dealt with and the shield Oath-Heart recovered. House Greywater escaped a Jotun execution squad into the marsh and now supports the Strong Reeds in resisting the Jotun.
t.Brocéliande: Queen Rhianos offered aid to anyone willing to discover what lies at the heart of the fallen city of Terunael in vallorn-infested Brocéliande.
t.Hahnmark: Every unquiet spirit haunting Turelva was laid to rest, and their stories were brought back to Anvil.
t.Holberg: The Wisdom assembly produced a practical solution to the curse on Holmauer Park, though not everyone in Holberg sees the cursed park as a problem.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: its Varushkan residents were named among those concerned with the lingering effects of the Great Storm.
t.Karsk: The self-styled Boyar of Isember was executed, a dark spirit was allowed to flee, and a kidnapped Navarr and relic were rescued from bandits. News also arrived of trouble involving the Mir Mozga.
t.Madruga: Its citizens were among those affected by the storm's aftermath, and trouble involving Calvos Sound was reported.
t.Ossium: The Druj destroyed two of the Bone Hives, which will produce nothing until after the Winter Solstice 384YE. Its residents were also affected by the storm's aftermath.
t.Otkodov: The Ambassador to Otkodov resolved the matter of the Thule warlock captured by the Jotun, earning the Thule's commendation.
t.Sarangrave: Imperial heroes could not reach the Bloodwater Spear orc held prisoner in the Dead Stone Woods, and Sarangrave's ghulai escaped Zenith with a mysterious text.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the shattering of its mirrors was noted as happening at the same time as the cursing of Holmauer Park.
t.Sea of Snow: The raid on Skallahn opened an opportunity for the Senate to commission large-scale maps of the waters near Jotun, Faraden and perhaps Thule lands.
t.Segura: A Grendel Waverider raiding party was prevented from reaching Cereva Hall after negotiations broke down.
t.Semmerholm: A grand audience with Barien at the Semmerstones went without significant hitches, and its Dawnish residents faced the aftermath of the Great Storm.
t.Sermersuaq: The hylje deepened their friendship with the Suaq after Koskinen's rescue, and the Thule warlock matter was resolved. The Jotun, however, kept the Spear of Bounty at Spirax wood.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the successful raid on Skallahn was cited as opening the Sea of Snow mapping opportunity and drawing Rhianos' attention.
t.Tassato: The city of Tassato was badly damaged by the surging waters of the Vassa during the Great Storm.
t.Temeschwar: An appraisal presented two extravagant possibilities for building a university in Temeschwar to increase the Empire's commissions.
t.The Barrens: Dawn's ambitions there drew Synod censure. Conjunctions claimed the Stone of Storms, saved Golden Axe soldiers and the Dawnish armies, cured the wagon raiders, and unleashed the Barren Sea.
t.The Semmerlak: The storm rains brought new opportunities to the Semmerlak.
t.Therunin: An expedition to an ancient wreck at the bottom of the Feverwater returned safely.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: it was tagged among the places affected by the storm's aftermath and by magical matters before the Conclave.
t.Zenith: The Highborn crusade trapped the Druj, but a Druj evil threatened to taint Zenith for years. The malaise at the Allied Groves was cured and the ex-prisoners restored, though Druj escaped with an amulet and a text.

r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Rhianos offered aid to those daring to find out what lies at the heart of the fallen city of Terunael.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: A practical solution, and an alternative suggestion, were put forward for the cursed Holmauer Park.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Mentioned in passing: news of trouble involving the Mir Mozga and Calvos Sound was noted among the visitors to Anvil.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Imperial heroes invoked magic at Saltmaw to unleash the Barren Sea on the Fangs and the Saltmarsh, and the sea now rages against the land.

384YE Autumn Equinox winds of war.d: In the west, Mathilda Fisher's orc allies took the Rushes and Gravenmarch in drought-stricken Bregasland. In Kahraman, Navarri armies forced the Lasambrian Jotun to retreat. An Imperial and Otkodov alliance broke the Jotun castles of Sermersuaq. Beyond the borders, heroes sealed the trogoni shaft beneath Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, a second raid ravaged Jotun Skallahn, and the Liberty Pact sacked Chalonsio. In the east, the Druj left Ossium for the Forest of Ulnak, the Barrens stayed quiet, and a hammer-and-anvil manoeuvre restored Zenith to Imperial hands, trapping the Druj in the south. Battle opportunities were offered in Kahraman, Sermersuaq and Zenith, alongside many conjunctions and military considerations.

n.Dawn: Dawn could field 40 force weight for the summit battles. Its armies remained barred from the Cautious Advance and Give Ground orders.
n.Druj: The Druj abandoned Ossium and lost Zenith to a decisive Imperial victory. Their armies there were trapped and cornered in the south, and their generals were gathering in Occursion.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, though a conjunction called Ash and Dust was offered in Screed in Spiral, a territory it shares with the Druj.
n.Highguard: Highborn armies could field 18 force weight and issue the Crusading Storm order. They gained bonuses when attacking into Zenith from Morrow or defending Morrow against attack from Zenith.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are listed with a force weight of 7 for the summit battles.
n.Jotun: The Jotun completed their hold on Bregasland through Mathilda Fisher, but their Lasambrians retreated in Kahraman and they were driven from Sermersuaq. Skallahn was also ravaged by a second Imperial raid.
n.Navarr: Navarri armies drove the Lasambrian invaders back in Kahraman, and Navarr could field 40 force weight. A conjunction was offered to rescue Navarri vates from Sarangrave.
n.The Brass Coast: Imperial armies forced the Lasambrian Jotun to retreat from the Cinnabar Hills of Kahraman after six months held back only by Fort Braydon. Conjunctions were offered in Gambit and in Calvos Sound in Madruga.
n.The Marches: Bregasland remained under Mathilda Fisher's rule, though Marchers there resisted her. Former Mournwold Marchers fought for the Lasambrians in Kahraman, and Marcher armies remained barred from the Give Ground order.
n.Thule: The Thule of Otkodov were allied with the Empire in breaking the Jotun hold on Sermersuaq. A battle opportunity was offered to stop Jotun champions unleashing vengeance against the Thule.
n.Urizen: Zenith was once again in Imperial hands after a decisive victory over the Druj, though the campaign remained on a knife's edge. The Citadel Guard was set to deteriorate again.
n.Varushka: The Druj withdrew from Ossium, leaving ruins behind, and conjunctions were offered in Ossium, Karsk and Volodmartz. Varushkan armies generated fewer victory points when campaigning alongside Brass Coast or Wintermark armies.
n.Wintermark: With Otkodov, the Empire finally liberated Sermersuaq, and raiders from Westerhal and Odd's End ravaged Skallahn. Wintermark could field the largest force weight at 51.

t.Bregasland: Under the great drought, Mathilda Fisher's orc allies seized the Rushes and Gravenmarch and dominated the marshes, though Marchers resisted. A conjunction was offered to eliminate a Jotun outpost in the Grey Fens.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: the Druj faded back into the Forest of Ulnak as they left Ossium.
t.Kahraman: The Lasambrian invaders were forced to retreat before Navarri armies, relieving the exhausted Fort Braydon garrison. A battle opportunity was offered to stop them recovering their casualties.
t.Karsk: A conjunction to Pyotr's Square in Lestazny was offered to investigate why the Ketsov of the Mir Mozga were acting strangely.
t.Madruga: A conjunction to Calvos in Calvos Sound was offered to lift spirits and investigate.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial army could take the Billet order in Mitwold.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Highborn or Urizen armies defending Morrow against attack from Zenith gained a defensive bonus.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian warriors in the Kahraman battle opportunity were formerly of Mournwold.
t.Ossium: The Druj left Ossium, fading back into the Forest of Ulnak and leaving ruins behind. A conjunction was offered to protect vital roads and bridges.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov was the Empire's ally in breaking the Jotun hold on Sermersuaq.
t.Sarangrave: A conjunction to Karliss in Whisperwood was offered to rescue Navarri vates.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Adamant Gate in Semmerholm could not be reduced below 1,000 military strength.
t.Sermersuaq: The Empire and Otkodov were to break Olgafsdottirshal and the Fortress of Kalant and finally liberate the territory. A battle opportunity and several conjunctions were offered there.
t.Skallahn: Raiders from Westerhal and Odd's End ravaged the Jarl of Kierheim's heartlands to break Jotun war capacity, while ships reaved the southern shores of Kalsea.
t.Spiral: A conjunction called Ash and Dust, at Kephalos' Delve in Screed, was offered to the Archmage of Night.
t.The Barrens: The Steel Causeway remained, unattacked, and the season was eerily quiet. Most Imperial armies fighting there suffered a penalty to territory conquered.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: any Imperial army could take the Billet order in Upwold.
t.Volodmartz: A conjunction titled All is Fair, All is Permitted was offered at Urodli's Fall in Brez.
t.Zenith: A hammer-and-anvil manoeuvre returned Zenith to Imperial hands and trapped the Druj armies in the south. A battle against gathering Druj generals and many conjunctions were offered.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Gravenmarch was seized by Mathilda Fisher's orc allies.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: A conjunction to Jayne's Top Copse was offered to eliminate a Jotun outpost.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: The Rushes were seized by Mathilda Fisher's orc allies.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: A conjunction to Talaeiros was offered to rescue the Damatian Cliffs forewoman, and a battle at Rojota Vantage to stop the Lasambrians recovering casualties.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: A conjunction to Calvos was offered to lift spirits and investigate.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: A conjunction to Petka's Path was offered to protect vital roads and bridges.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: A conjunction to Karliss was offered to rescue Navarri vates.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: thunder rolled through the Silver Peaks as the alliance faced the last Jotun castles.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Conjunctions were offered to recover the relic Tuuli's Eye at Avointaivas and to rescue Yanti the Storm Runner at Flat Hills.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: A battle at Jaelwif's Mound was offered to stop Jotun revenge on the Thule, and a conjunction at Kilpailuala Bay to send Jarl Snekmar to the Howling Abyss.
r.Spiral/Screed: A conjunction called Ash and Dust was offered at Kephalos' Delve.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: A conjunction to the Aurelius Estates was offered to summon Sorin's hungry wolves to the Barrens.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: A conjunction titled All is Fair, All is Permitted was offered at Urodli's Fall.
r.Zenith/Iteri: A conjunction to the Pallasian Steps was offered to destroy miasma pillars and exorcise tortured souls.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Conjunctions were offered to slay the Endless Stalker at the Rift in the Veil and to destroy miasma pillars at the Spire of Twisting Shadow.
r.Zenith/Occursion: A battle was offered against the gathering of Druj generals, with conjunctions at the Tower of the Fall and the Field of Celestial Mist.
r.Zenith/Proceris: A conjunction to the Plantation of Tall Ferns was offered to destroy miasma pillars and intercept marshlings.

A wandering fire.d: The Bloodcloaks, Green Shield, Drakes, Bounders and Tusks, with three Thule armies and hylje aid, besieged Olgafsdottirshal. The Drakes breached its gates in the second week, though Eisa Winterborn's yegarra held long enough for hundreds of Jotun to escape to Kalant. The Golden Sun then arrived by forced march, and on the fourth day of the Kalant siege Thule warlocks blasted open the gates. Around fifteen hundred alliance soldiers fell. The Shard of Winter seized wealth and thralls, later ransoming them back to the Jotun. The Thule outlawed slavery and asked for help stopping a Jotun ritual to Hayaak at Jaelwif's Mound.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun crossed the Empire by Autumn-enchanted forced march and arrived at Kalant, lifting Imperial spirits and helping to bring down the last Jotun refuge in Sermersuaq.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Tusks fought in the conquest of Sermersuaq, expecting Wintermark to repay them in Bregasland. Jarl Snekmar also demanded that Imperial Orcs join the warriors sent to face him in a final battle.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost both great citadels and every region of Sermersuaq, falling back to Skallahn. Some fought on, with a ritual to Hayaak against the Thule, Jarl Snekmar's death-seeking warband, and a pursuit of Wintermark raiders.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm withdrew east to Skarsind through the forests of Hercynia.
n.Thule: Three Thule armies fought alongside the Empire, and their warlocks opened Kalant's gates. The Shard of Winter angered Imperial soldiers by seizing wealth and thralls and ransoming them to the Jotun. The Dragons then outlawed slavery and pleaded for help against Hayaak's heralds.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks and the Green Shield, who paid heavily for leading the assault on Olgafsdottirshal, helped make Sermersuaq fully Imperial again. Wintermark now has opportunities to recover Tuuli's Eye and to answer Jarl Snekmar's challenge.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher armies had just left Bregasland, and the Bounders and Tusks expected their northern allies to help retake it in return.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm had to travel through Hercynia's rugged forests because the western end of Pakaanan's Pass had been collapsed.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: more than twenty thousand Thule warriors came out of Otkodov, and the Ambassador to Otkodov received the Thule plea for help.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was entirely retaken, with the rank two fortifications Olgafsdottirshal and Kalant now in Imperial hands. Jotun remnants, a ritual threat and a mysterious pursuer still trouble the territory.
t.Skallahn: The defeated Jotun retreated into Skallahn, while a successful Wintermark raid there brought back much wealth but left one group pursued back to the border.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm withdrew east to Skarsind.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: Igya Olgafsdottir, builder of the Sermersuaq citadels, is named as eldest child of the Jarl of Tromsa.

r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: the garrison of the Thule Citadel of Silver and Bone, which dominates the Silver Peaks, supported the alliance armies.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The Fortress of Kalant fell on the fourth day of the siege, ending Jotun control of Stark. Conjunctions to Avointaivas and the Flat Hills offer the chance to recover Tuuli's Eye and to intercept a creature pursuing Wintermark raiders.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Olgafsdottirshal fell after the Drakes breached its gates and is now an Imperial bastion. Tanikipari also hosts the Jotun ritual at Jaelwif's Mound and Jarl Snekmar's raiding camp above Kilpailuala Bay.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Mentioned in passing: the surviving Jotun forces retreated into Iron Stand after Kalant fell.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun had collapsed the western end of the pass, forcing the Summer Storm to take a longer route.

A yellow star hung.d: Fortifications rose in Ossium's Drownbark Forest and in Operus, Caeli, Serra Briante and Clypion, and Penumbral Veils lingered over Ossium, Madruga, Kahraman, the Barrens and Zenith. The Navarr and the Citadel Guard restored Zenith's trods. Regrow the Land's Heart aided Iteri and western Clypion, but a curse cut Zenith's herb harvests. Storms blamed on the Archmage of Spring battered the Barrens. Weirwater's horse-lovers shared a stormy dream, and artists dreamt of Farren Silver Streams. The Key grew ascendant. Conjunctions were identified to Kephalos' Delve in Screed, where Grendel sky mages were exploring, and to Udoli's Fall in Brez. Olic gave Urizen the Concordance of Earthbound Stars, and Treacher's Quill also entered Urizen lore.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Weirwater saw everyone with an affinity for horses dream of riding a galloping horse along a storm-lashed shore. They woke exhilarated, though the dream taught them nothing new about horses.
n.Druj: Veils still shroud the Druj-held Barrens and Zenith, but the Barrens were battered by storms. The Zenith herb curse hurt the orcs most, and their hold in Iteri and western Clypion was described as weakened.
n.Grendel: A group of Grendel sky mages with mercenary escorts pressed deep into the Black Plateau in Screed and has not returned. A conjunction offers Imperial heroes the chance to discover what they are doing.
n.Navarr: Working with the General of the Citadel Guard, the Navarr successfully performed the Dance of Navarr and Thorn, restoring the trods of Zenith.
n.The Brass Coast: A Frozen Citadel was summoned in Serra Briante, and Penumbral Veils continue to hang over the Freeborn territories of Madruga and Kahraman.
n.Urizen: Urizen gained Frozen Citadels in Morrow and Zenith, restored trods and rejuvenating rains that gave hope to its people in Zenith, though Zenith's herb gardens were cursed. Five new rituals entered Urizen lore, including the Concordance of Earthbound Stars and Treacher's Quill.
n.Varushka: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen now protect Ossium from the Druj, and a veil still hangs over that territory. A conjunction to monster-haunted ruins in Brez was entrusted to the Boyar of the Sovereign's Head.

t.Kahraman: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Serra Briante, and a Penumbral Veil continues to hinder divination into the territory.
t.Madruga: A Penumbral Veil still hangs over Madruga, so rituals scrying into it must first overcome the veil.
t.Morrow: Frozen Citadels were summoned from the Summer realm in both Operus and Caeli.
t.Ossium: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose in the Drownbark Forest to help protect Ossium from the Druj, and a Penumbral Veil remains over the territory.
t.Spiral: Grendel sky mages were tracked exploring the Black Plateau in Screed, and a conjunction to Kephalos' Delve was identified for an Imperial expedition.
t.The Barrens: Dreadful storms and waves pummelled every region bordering the Barren Sea, likely blunting the Fangs and flooding Saltmarsh. A veil also still shrouds the territory.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: some Weirwater horse dreams involved diving beneath its waters to sunken ruins, possibly linked to strange treasures left on its shores.
t.Volodmartz: A conjunction to Udoli's Fall, among long-forgotten ruins in the far north of the territory, was identified. Travellers there face early snows and monsters.
t.Weirwater: Everyone in Weirwater with an interest in horses dreamt vividly of riding on a stormy, moonless shore, and woke full of wonder.
t.Zenith: Zenith gained a Frozen Citadel, restored trods and muted rejuvenating rains, while its herb gardens suffered a curse that cut their yields. A veil still hangs over it.

r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: One of the Frozen Citadels was summoned from the Summer realm in Serra Briante.
r.Morrow/Caeli: A Frozen Citadel was summoned in Caeli during the Summer Solstice.
r.Morrow/Operus: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Operus.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen rose in the Drownbark Forest, helping protect Ossium from the Druj.
r.Spiral/Screed: A group of Grendel sky mages pushed into Kephalos' Delve on the Black Plateau, and Imperial heroes may travel there by conjunction to investigate.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Bitter Strand bore some of the worst of the storms, with thunder, lightning, mighty waves and even waterspouts.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: Saltmarsh was among the hardest-hit regions in the storms and is likely to have been flooded.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: A conjunction to Udoli's Fall in Brez at 20:45 on Saturday will take heroes to ruins sheltering travellers, where the risk from monsters is high.
r.Zenith/Clypion: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Clypion with the Citadel Guard's aid. The restorative rains encouraged new growth and hope in western Clypion, where the Druj hold has weakened.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The rejuvenating rains were felt most strongly in Iteri, encouraging healthy growth and giving the remaining Urizen hope as the Druj hold weakened.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The enchantment brought a burst of growth to the marshes of Proceris, with bright flowers springing up between octopus-haunted pools and ruined cisterns.

Archive:Paid Work Autumn Equinox 384YE.d: The page is a roster rather than an account of events. It sets out three unlabelled tables of citizens, each entry giving a name and an Imperial nation. Dawn, Highguard, the Imperial Orcs, Navarr, the Brass Coast, the League, the Marches, Urizen, Varushka and Wintermark all appear. The first table is dominated by Brass Coast and Navarr names. The second is overwhelmingly Navarr, with sizeable Dawn and Wintermark contingents. The third is a short list of a few Dawn, League, Marcher and Wintermark citizens. The page does not explain what distinguishes the three tables, nor what work was done or what was paid.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish citizens appear in all three tables of those who took paid work, including a sizeable group in the second.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named on the page; the only link is Zenith, which appears in the names of Urizen citizens.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn citizens are listed in the first and second tables, among them Lazarus of the Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: a group of Imperial Orc citizens, including several Bloodcrows, appears in the first table only.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr citizens make up a large share of the first table and the great majority of the second.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Brass Coast citizens form the largest group in the first table, with one more listed in the second.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: League citizens, many styled after Sarvos, Temeschwar, Tassato or Holberg, appear in all three tables.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Marcher citizens are listed in all three tables, most numerously in the second.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen citizens are listed in the first and second tables, including two named as being of Zenith Ascendant.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushkan citizens appear in the first and second tables.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark citizens appear in all three tables, with many Dunning and Dunwolf names in the second.

t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the territory appears only in the name of the Highborn citizen Lazarus of the Necropolis.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos appears only in the names of several League citizens, such as Achille di Sarvos.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar appears only in the names of several League citizens, such as Aleksei Dukov van Temeschwar.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Zenith appears only in the names of two Urizen citizens styled 'of Zenith Ascendant'.

Back in the same place.d: Temeschwar's existing faculties of metallurgy, mining and warding did not suit the Senate's brief, but its merchant princes backed a grander plan. A new university building (60 wains of white granite, 30 of weirwood, 180 crowns, six months, in Hanuri) would create the Master of Rings. This national League title, appointed by the Bourse, could announce one extra civilian commission each season and would be charged with enriching the League. Separately, if the Synod recognised La Volpe as an exemplar of Ambition (or Pride), the Senate could build his tomb, creating the Blood Red Builder to commission great works or tombs. Both opportunities lapse after the Summer Solstice 385YE. Graciana would be on leave for the following season.

n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the prognosticator Graciana i Lòpez i Guerra is granted leave to travel home to Madruga for her niece's wedding, so she will be unavailable until the Winter Solstice 384YE.
n.The League: The League stands to gain a national title, the Master of Rings, charged with generating wealth for the League, and the Blood Red Builder could also become a League national position appointed by its National Assembly.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: materials passing through Temeschwar from Varushka are one source of the white granite, mithril and weirwood the Master of Rings would receive.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg's university is described as the Empire's foremost centre of engineering learning, the standard a new Temeschwar university would seek to rival.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Graciana returns home to Madruga to oversee arrangements for her niece Ailande's wedding.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is named as a city whose university prestige, and whose supposed condescension towards Temeschwar, the new university would answer.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwari believe folk in Tassato look down on them, a resentment the proposed university is meant to address.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's merchant princes offered endowments and contributions to back a new university and the Master of Rings, and its citizens called for a tomb honouring La Volpe, both to establish the city as the equal of its League rivals.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Hanuri would host both proposed commissions: the new University of Temeschwar, built on demolished slums on the city's north side, and Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar's inspirational tomb bearing the Butchers' Bank symbol.

Beyond this dark house.d: The Gryphon's Pride, Northern Eagle and Iron Helms pushed into the Echofell while two Thule armies from Otkodov held defensive positions alongside the garrison of Flajokep. The Druj had already gone. The Imperial forces, helped by magical defences in the Drownbark Forest, mopped up the remaining raiders, though the region stayed under threat. The Thule then returned to the Bonewood. Druj damage to the Bone Hives during the Summer Solstice means the Keeper of the Bonehives receives no production until Spring 385YE. Lise de Lionsgate has proposed rebuilding the ruined tower as the Tower of the Manticore. A conjunction on Petka's Path offers a chance to stop Druj sappers before the Drownbark Forest becomes contested.

n.Druj: The Druj armies abandoned Ossium after destroying the Tower of the Scorpion and retreated into the Forest of Ulnak. Their raiders still lurk in the Drownbark and Echofell, and a band of sappers is tearing up roads and bridges along Petka's Path.
n.Thule: Two Thule orc armies marched out of Otkodov to defend Ossium alongside the garrison of Flajokep, aiding the humans as the Dragons willed. They then returned to the Bonewood once the territory was secured.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle and Iron Helms helped restore Imperial control of the Echofell, but Varushkan hold on the Drownbark is threatened by Druj sabotage. The Keeper of the Bonehives will receive no production until Spring 385YE because of the earlier Druj attack on the hives.

t.Forest of Ulnak: The Druj armies withdrew from Ossium back into the shadowed depths of the Forest of Ulnak, from where they continue to threaten Ossium's eastern borders.
t.Ossium: With the Druj armies gone, Ossium was largely secured, though raiders remain in its eastern regions. A proposal to rebuild the ruined tower as the Tower of the Manticore would add a fortification on its eastern border.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the two Thule orc armies that went to defend Ossium marched out of Otkodov.

r.Ossium/Bonewood: Mentioned in passing: the Thule returned to the Bonewood once Ossium was as secure as it could be.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Magical defences here helped Imperial forces deal with raiders, but Druj sappers are now wrecking roads and bridges on Petka's Path. A conjunction offers a chance to stop them; if they are not stopped, the region will become contested.
r.Ossium/Echofell: The Imperial armies found the Druj gone from the Echofell and quickly brought it back under Imperial control, though it remains under threat. The proposed Tower of the Manticore would permanently remove that threat.
r.Ossium/Nearweald: Mentioned in passing: Petka's Path, the road being sabotaged by the Druj, links the southern coast through to the Nearweald.

Brightness long ago.d: Commissioned by Sagua i Ezmara, Master of the Koboldi, the warded seal was carried down through natural caverns, unstable Terunael mineworkings, vast runecarved trollworkings and finally the trogoni burrows, facing trogoni hulks, strange new trogoni breeds, constructs, unliving spirits and runic traps. The seal was set just as an immense trogoni rose up the shaft, and the swarms fled; a brief Deepest Feast followed. The koboldi shared the principles of the ward so similar seals can protect mines and mana sites across the Empire. Participants won orichalcum, weltsilver, tempest jade, crystal mana, mithril and ilium rings, the Delver of the Depths gains deeper access, and a new Explore the Depths action opened.

n.Dawn: Urged on by their assembly, dozens of Dawnish captains joined the delve, their reckless knightly inspiration greatly increasing the treasure won, and Dawnish units may now take Explore the Depths as freely as bordering nations despite not neighbouring the sinkhole.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: two Highborn captains appear on the list of expedition participants.
n.Navarr: Answering their assembly's call, Navarr sent the largest contingent, uncovered hidden Terunael chambers on the edge of Miaren, and earned a report on their ancestors' work there for the Advisor on the Vallorn; Navarr units may also now Explore the Depths.
n.The League: Numerous League captains, many from Temeschwar, joined the expedition, and League military units can now take the Explore the Depths action to recover metals and crystal mana.
n.The Marches: A few Marcher captains and a unit of shadowy warriors raised from beneath the trees of the Marches joined the delve, and Marcher units may now Explore the Depths.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: a single Urizen captain is listed among the expedition's participants.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: a single Varushkan captain is listed among the expedition's participants.
n.Wintermark: Having declared the endeavour heroic, Wintermark sent many captains and a unit of shadowy warriors; its runesmiths identified the ancient tunnels as remarkably preserved trollworkings, yielding runic secrets for future opportunities at the Runegrott Runeforge, and its units may now Explore the Depths.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is now safe from a trogoni host pouring out of the sinkhole, and explorers believe the vast ancient trollworkings may stretch beneath its mountains.
t.Miaren: Miaren is spared the threatened trogoni devastation, and newly found Terunael chambers on its edge shed light on what the ancient Navarr dug for there.
t.Temeschwar: With the seal in place, Temeschwar no longer faces a swarm of trogoni rising from the neighbouring sinkhole to ravage its mines and mana sites.
t.Upwold: Upwold is freed from the threat of trogoni bursting out of Lorenzo's Deep Pockets to devastate its lands.

Construct Black Canal.d: Proposed by Upwold's senator and seconded by Bastion's, the motion passed at no cost in thrones; the canal followed the Light upon the water Wind of Fortune. It required 60 wains of white granite, 40 wains of weirwood, 200 crowns and nine months, all met through many private donations from 384YE to 386YE. The Mournwold orcs supplied half the labour costs (100 crowns) through money, food and work, and grew more familiar to the northern Marches. The canal raised investment in Mitwold's farms and businesses and the Mournwold's businesses and mines. After the Jotun conquest of the Mourn in Summer 386YE, the Mournwold half gave no benefit and Mitwold's yield fell to 18 rings.

n.Jotun: The Jotun conquest of the Mourn after the Summer Solstice 386YE stripped away the Mournwold half of the canal's benefit and sharply cut the return to Mitwold.
n.The Marches: The Marches gained a canal joining its two most prosperous settlements, Meade and Sarcombe, funded by many Marcher donors and built alongside the Mournwold orcs, who became better known to the northern Marches.

t.Mitwold: Mitwold's farms and businesses gained greater investment from the canal starting at Meade, though after the Mourn's loss its half yields only 18 rings until Chalkdowns and Southmoor are reclaimed.
t.Mournwold: The canal reached Sarcombe and raised investment in the Mournwold's businesses and mines, with the local orcs paying half the labour, but the Jotun conquest left its Mournwold half providing no benefit.

r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: Chalkdowns must be reclaimed from the Jotun before the canal's Mitwold half can return to its full benefit.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Southmoor's recovery is, alongside Chalkdowns, a condition for the canal again yielding its full benefit.

Construct Boar's Market.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Casinea, the motion took up an opportunity set out in the Good old smooth red wine Wind of Fortune. It passed at 50 thrones. The commission cost 12 wains of weirwood and 24 crowns and would take three months. After the Autumn Equinox 384YE, Bertrand provided 3 thrones and 12 wains of weirwood towards it. Once complete, the market-fayre would be overseen by a new Imperial title, the Reeve of Boar's Market. The title was intended for a yeofolk and appointed by Tally of the Votes, though the motion's own text described election by well worn path.

n.Dawn: Dawn would gain a market through which it could buy weirwood, mithril and white granite. It would also gain a new Dawnish title, the Reeve of Boar's Market, intended for one of its yeofolk.

t.Astolat: The Boar's Market was to be built at Boar's Hollow in Astolat. Bertrand supplied the thrones and weirwood after the Autumn Equinox to begin its construction.

Construct Giritane's Gaze.d: Commissioned under the Stone and stone Wind of Fortune, the great work cost 40 wains of white granite and 80 crowns in gold and jewels, and took three months to construct. Enchanter Baldwin, senator of Weirwater, agreed to provide the funding. Contributions came from many donors between Autumn 384YE and Summer 385YE, including all 40 wains of granite from Meliodas Cambrerius. The completed Alabaster Owlbeast stands on a hill in Wickmoor, north-west of the Weirwater Vales, harnessing the power of a Summer regio, with two massive lightstones making it visible at night. It gives every mine in Weirwater a share in a bounty of 900 rings in precious metals and gemstones.

n.Dawn: Dawn's territory of Weirwater gained an immense mandowla colossus, funded with the agreement of its senator, Enchanter Baldwin, and supported by many donors. Its completion brings extra wealth to every Dawnish mine in the territory.

t.Weirwater: Every mine in Weirwater now receives a share in a bounty of 900 rings in precious metals and gemstones, on top of the magical materials the mines already produce.

r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: The white stone Alabaster Owlbeast was raised on a hill in Wickmoor, north-west of the Weirwater Vales, where it harnesses a Summer regio. Its two great lightstones make it especially visible at night.

Construct Great Library of Hacynian.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Therunin, the motion commissioned the expansion of the Library of Hacynian into the Great Library, leaving the title 'Advisor on the Vallorn' unchanged. Navarr asked the Senate to disburse funds for the commission, which cost 50 wains of white granite, 40 of weirwood, 30 of mithril and 240 crowns, and takes a year to complete. The motion passed. After the Autumn Equinox most materials and much of the money came from Nemae Splitroot, with further contributions from many others. Once complete, the library would allow research into a way to finally defeat the vallorn, and League and Highguard mandates were passed to support it.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: a Highguard mandate (Mandate 50) was passed to support the vallorn research the library would enable.
n.Navarr: Navarr requested Senate funding for a library its people had waited generations for, and many Navarr contributed materials and coin, chiefly Nemae Splitroot, in hope of finding a way to finally defeat the vallorn.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the senator for Therunin seconded the motion, and Edric of Urizen donated a crown towards it.

t.Hercynia: The Library of Hacynian in Hercynia was commissioned to be expanded into the Great Library, a year-long construction intended to collate vallorn lore from across the world.

Construct Hall of the Unbroken.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Astolat, the motion commissioned a mana sinecure as part of the Proffered Hand Network. Its stated purpose is to provide physical and emotional healing to former slaves and to rehabilitate them into the Way and the Empire. Construction requires 12 wains of mithril, 3 thrones in labour and three months. After the Autumn Equinox, Lady Eleanor Novarion provided the 12 wains of mithril and 2 thrones 6 crowns, and Ergot Di Cevia and Fintan Nighthaven each gave a crown. Once complete, it is intended to provide mana to the Hearthtender of the Unbroken, a title appointed by unanimous decision of Wintermark's senators.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a new sinecure title, the Hearthtender of the Unbroken, which its senators will appoint by unanimous decision and which is intended to receive the Hall's mana once it is built.

t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq's senator proposed the motion, and the territory is to host a sanctuary for former slaves within the Proffered Hand Network.

r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The East Floes is the chosen site for the Hall of the Unbroken, which is due to take three months to build once its materials and labour are supplied.

Construct Kostjyas Respite.d: The commission followed the Thousands or more Wind of Fortune. It cost 30 wains of white granite, 30 wains of weirwood and 144 crowns, raised from 120 because Ossium was under-developed, and took six months to build. Kostjya, Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov and others supplied the money and materials after the Autumn Equinox and Winter Solstice 384YE. The town occupies the cove from which the Druj once launched rafts against Semmerholm. Once complete, it removes the Bittershore's under-developed quality and adds 20 thrones a season in taxes, spread across the Semmerlak territories. It also creates the title of Merchant-boyar of Bittershore and opens opportunities to expand docks around the lake.

n.Dawn: Once the port was complete, an option would be offered to expand the docks at Lacre in Dawn's territory of Semmerholm, and Dawn's Semmerlak lands would share in the increased taxation.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the new town occupies the cove from which the Druj launched rafts to attack Semmerholm during Empress Varkula's reign.
n.The League: The new port might later allow a similar dock in Holberg's Misericorde or Utterlund, spreading Holberg's wealth across the Semmerlak.
n.Varushka: A Varushkan project, self-funded by Cabal Lyktan and Varushkan contributors. It developed Ossium's Bittershore, created a new Merchant-boyar title and opened dock opportunities at Korotny and Ivarsgard.

t.Holberg: Once the port was complete, there would be a possibility of building a similar dock in Misericorde or Utterlund, letting Holberg's wealth spread across the Semmerlak.
t.Karov: The completed port would open an option to expand the docks at Korotny in Karov, and Karov would share in the extra taxation from the Semmerlak.
t.Karsk: The completed port would open an option to expand the docks at Ivarsgard in Karsk, which would also share in the new Semmerlak taxation.
t.Ossium: Ossium gained the new port-town of Kostjyas Respite on the Bittershore, which cost extra crowns to build because the territory was under-developed.
t.Semmerholm: The town stands in the cove once used by the Druj to raid Semmerholm, and its completion would open an option to expand the docks at Lacre.
t.The Semmerlak: The new port on the lake's shores would raise Imperial taxation by 20 thrones a season, spread among the territories bordering the Semmerlak, and encourage further docks around it.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: Once Kostjyas Respite was complete, a similar dock might be built in Misericorde, linking it to trade across the Semmerlak.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Once Kostjyas Respite was complete, a similar dock might be built in Utterlund, linking it to trade across the Semmerlak.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Kostjyas Respite was built here, removing the Bittershore's under-developed quality and creating the Merchant-boyar of Bittershore to oversee the port's prosperity.

Construct Potato Fields of Happiston.d: Proposed by the senator for Mournwold and seconded by Ossium, the motion commissioned a mana crystal sinecure at Happiston. It was to be fully funded by the Happiston Volunteers, and its keeper was to be appointed with tenure by unanimous decision of the Marcher senators. The motion gave no size or cost, so the civil service assumed the minimum of 10 wains. Alan Sheppard provided 12 wains of mithril and 2 thrones 6 crowns, and Ergot Di Cevia provided 2 crowns. The missing details about the sinecure's nature and cost were supplied after the Winter Solstice 384YE. The commission was then completed, with the Keeper of the Happiston Fields to be appointed at the Spring Equinox 385YE.

n.The Marches: The Marcher senators gained the right to appoint, by unanimous decision, a tenured keeper to a new mana-producing title in one of their own territories.

t.Mournwold: Mournwold's senator proposed the motion, which gave this Marcher territory a new mana sinecure at Happiston, completed in time for its keeper to be appointed at the Spring Equinox 385YE.

r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Prosperous Potato Fields of Happiston were built at Happiston in the Chalkdowns, funded by the Happiston Volunteers, as a sinecure intended to provide mana to its keeper.

Construct Reapers' Repose.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Semmerholm, the motion commissioned the Reapers' Repose for 10 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns, taking three months. Laughlan Vi Temeschwar provided the materials and money after the Autumn Equinox. The civil service believed it related to the proposal by Sovia Lahm von Temeschwar, Merchant-prince of the Emerald Magpie Guild, in the A health to the company Wind of Fortune. On that assumption the Chatelaine, appointed by unanimous decision of the League senators, receives 16 crowns each season, unlimited access to the restful sanctuary and three doses of Tranquil Nostrum. Construction was completed, with the first appointment due at the Winter Solstice 384YE.

n.The League: The League's senators gained a new sinecure to bestow by unanimous decision, with the first Chatelaine of the Reapers' Repose due to be appointed at the Winter Solstice 384YE.

t.Temeschwar: The Reapers' Repose was built in Melfort, Temeschwar, with Laughlan Vi Temeschwar supplying the white granite, weirwood and money, and it is thought to stem from a proposal by the Temeschwar merchant-prince Sovia Lahm von Temeschwar.

Construct Scholars of the Sword Academy.d: The announcement, made in Autumn 384YE under an Imperial Wayleave, commissioned a sinecure whose custodian would be titled the Master of Defence of the Scholars of the Sword Academy. Because the announcement omitted cost details, the Civil Service assumed the minimum size of 10 wains. Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided 2 thrones, 4 crowns and 10 wains of white granite after the Autumn Equinox. The completed sinecure creates an Imperial title with tenure, appointed by unanimous decision of the League's senators, which receives a regular stipend from the college. The first Master of Defence was due to be elected at the Winter Solstice 384YE.

n.The League: The League gains a new Imperial title with tenure, the Master of Defence of the Scholars of the Sword Academy, to be appointed by unanimous decision of its senators, with the first election due at the Winter Solstice 384YE.

t.Holberg: The Scholars of the Sword Academy, a white granite sinecure, was built in the city of Holberg, and its custodian will draw a regular stipend from the college.

Construct Swords of Nearweald.d: The motion passed at 150 Thrones and authorised construction of a fortified barracks requiring 30 wains of mithril, 20 wains of weirwood and 120 crowns in labour, raised from 100 because Ossium was under-developed. It took three months to build and carries an upkeep of 5 Thrones each season. Pavuk Vid Strascovich supplied the mithril, Vesna Borkovna Prochnost provided 20 wains of weirwood and 14 thrones 7 crowns, and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave a crown. Once complete, it removed the underpopulated quality from Nearweald. While the upkeep is paid, it gives Varushkan armies in Ossium an additional defending order, Hospitality of the Boyars, and allows Varushkan armies to be raised in Ossium in nine months rather than a year.

n.Varushka: Varushkan citizens supplied the mithril, weirwood and funds for the barracks, and while its upkeep is paid Varushkan armies in Ossium gain the Hospitality of the Boyars defending order and can be raised there in nine months rather than a year.

t.Ossium: The Swords of Nearweald were built in Ossium at a higher labour cost because of the territory's under-developed state, and the barracks now strengthens the raising and defence of Varushkan armies there.

r.Ossium/Nearweald: The barracks stands in Nearweald, and its completion removed the region's underpopulated quality.

Construct Western Kalsea Spy Network.d: The commission followed up the opportunity created by the successful Skallahn raid, as set out in the Take it further wind of fortune. It required 5 wains of weirwood, 10 crowns and three months to build, with an upkeep of 5 thrones each season. After the Autumn Equinox several Imperial citizens contributed funds: Cpt. Hendrick van Hoven and Tevoro von Ghurayb von Holberg gave 2 crowns 10 rings each, and Ergot Di Cevia, Fintan Nighthaven and Æðelric Dagursson gave 1 crown each. The network did not survive. Jarl Ustigar of Kierheim's forces destroyed it, using information gathered when they destroyed the Skallahn spy network.

n.Jotun: The network was meant to give the Empire an edge in its offensive against the Jotun. Jarl Ustigar of Kierheim's forces destroyed it, turning intelligence from the earlier Skallahn spy network against the Imperial spies.

t.Skallahn: The successful raid on Jotun-held Skallahn opened the way for this network further west. Its downfall began in Skallahn, where the destruction of the Skallahn spy network yielded the information the Jotun used to find and destroy the new one.

Create Chair of the Wolf.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Holberg, the motion acted on the A health to the company wind of fortune. It passed, and expansion of the Holberg Guild of Engineers began. The new Chair of the Wolf can announce a commission (a great work, ministry, sinecure or folly) provided it takes place entirely within a League territory, and this does not count against the limited number of commissions the Empire can undertake each season. As part of creating the title, the League commissioned four impressive structures, one in each of its cities. The arrangement differs from the original Winter 383YE proposal but is fully endorsed by the Guild of Engineers.

n.The League: The League gains a new national title, the Chair of the Wolf, chosen by Tally of the Votes and able to commission projects within League territory outside the Empire's usual limit, along with four impressive structures, one in each of its cities.

t.Holberg: Holberg's Guild of Engineers has begun expanding its premises, and the territory's senator seconded the motion creating the Chair of the Wolf.

Dear green space.d: Restoring the park would mean destroying all vegetation and sculpture (20 wains of weirwood, 10 of white granite, 160 crowns, nine months) and closing the Wunderkind Woods regio with Wind of Mundane Silence. Sofia Rebeshi's coven offered to cast it in return for the cursed lumber, giving three foci to the Conclave. Tharim offered to lift the curse for two more years of amity, but would take the orchard and Flowers memorial too. Restoration ends the Pavilion's aura, though true liao might reconsecrate it. Alternatively, a ministry could create the Tender of the Blood Orchard title selling Winter vis and staffs, or a mithril great work could gate the park for business income. The two approaches are mutually exclusive.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn business folk are credited with keeping the park's waters safe, and the Highborn are said to be wary of taking a Winter herald at his word.
n.The League: Holberg's burghers must choose between costly restoration and embracing their cursed park; the League Assembly could reconsecrate the Pavilion with true liao, and the proposed Tender of the Blood Orchard would most suitably be a League national title.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Memorial Garden, with its orchard and memorial to General Flowers, survived the curse but would be destroyed if Tharim's offer were accepted unrenegotiated.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: in the fiction a Holberg man recalls his childhood vow to study astronomancy in Urizen.

t.Holberg: Holberg faces a choice between restoring its cursed park as a great work or accepting the curse, with options for a Winter vis ministry, a new Imperial title, or a gated park sharing 743 rings a season with local businesses.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the curse fell as Sarvos's mirrors shattered, and a Sarvosan sage and Sarvosan fright-pamphlets are referenced.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Tharim's herald Obligatus at the Copse of the Bone Birch in Upwold confirmed the Bound King's offer to lift the curse.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Mentioned in passing: the clocks of Holfried are heard striking midnight in the in-character story.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer Park is the subject of every proposal: tearing out the cursed woods and closing the regio, letting Tharim strip it, harvesting the Blood Orchard, or gating it for paying visitors, with the Pavilion's aura lost if the curse is lifted.

Down the cavalier road.d: Eleonaris accepted her ceded statue, which became a mist-shrouded island in the Semmerlak. She still forbade Knights of Glory but promised Brother Luke a replacement ritual at the Winter Solstice. Jaheris sent two heralds to the Icy Crag, speeding curse research. Cathan Canae remained angered by the Empire's surrender of land. Hayaak, blaming Edric du Gauvain (dead since 381YE) for his fall, demanded the knight's head. He reinforced the Jotun, loosed gryphons in Coombe and worked to turn Eleonaris against the Empire. Dawn has until Summer 385YE to win eternals' favour, through statues or negotiation, and so make the Eastern Sky Favoured.

n.Dawn: Dawn's enchanters were offered the chance to make the Eastern Sky a Favoured army under up to five Summer eternals, with Eleonaris already willing. Meanwhile Hayaak's monsters menace Astolat and he demands the head of the long-dead Dawnish knight Edric du Gauvain.
n.Druj: The Druj hold Dawnguard, where Cathan Canae insists her statue be raised in the ruined Towers of the Dawn, meaning Dawn would have to take the region from them to win her favour.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae cited the ceding of two territories to the Grendel as an example of the Empire's failure to defend its land.
n.Jotun: The Jotun gained significant reinforcements and a powerful ally, as Hayaak's feathered heralds joined their forces and he vowed to support them on every battlefield against the Empire until he receives Edric du Gauvain's head.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's heralds continue to work with Imperial citizens at the College of Engineering in the League's territory of Temeschwar.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae decried regions of Varushka given up to buy Thule support, and Meraud is said to show some slight interest in the Thule but offer them little patronage.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the surrender of entire regions of Varushka to the Thule is one of the losses that angered Cathan Canae.

t.Astolat: Hayaak's gryphons and other beasts now stalk the forests of Coombe. Adamant and Meraud have proposed statues at the Castle of Thorns and in Weaving as the price of their favour for the Eastern Sky.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Rhianos wants his statue ceded to him so that he can watch brave Dawnish knights try their hands in the forests of Brocéliande.
t.Semmerholm: Barien has asked for a statue at the Semmerstones and Rhianos for one at Racqueen as the price of their favour for the Eastern Sky.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the recent Imperial raid on Skallahn is among the bold adventures that delighted Rhianos.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: a House deCassilon representative brought the news that sparked Nimue's negotiations back to Spiral Castle from Anvil.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Adamant's heralds continue to work with Imperial citizens at the College of Engineering in Temeschwar.
t.The Barrens: Cathan Canae will only accept a statue in the ruins of the Towers of the Dawn in the Barrens, which she regards as Dawn's rightful dominion lost to the Druj.
t.The Semmerlak: The waters of the Semmerlak rose around Eleonaris's statue, turning its promontory into a fog-shrouded island guarded by sharp hidden rocks.
t.Weirwater: Jaheris's heralds suggested a statue of the Unicorn Prince beside the Weirwater Vales, though he would accept another suitably storied site.

r.Astolat/Coombe: Gryphons and other monsters sent by Hayaak now prowl Coombe's forests, attacking travellers bound for Caer Faucon and forcing armed patrols into the woods.
r.Semmerholm/Elvette: The page names Semmerholm, without singling out this region, as the proposed site of statues to Barien at the Semmerstones and Rhianos at Racqueen, should Dawn seek their favour.
r.Semmerholm/Ulvenholm: The page names Semmerholm, without singling out this region, as the proposed site of statues to Barien at the Semmerstones and Rhianos at Racqueen, should Dawn seek their favour.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Cathan Canae demands her statue stand in the ruined Towers of the Dawn in Dawnguard, so the Empire would have to reconquer the region from the Druj to gain her favour.

Good old smooth red wine.d: Building on the wealth brought by the Blood Red Roads, four projects were proposed. The first was a Boar's Hollow market-fayre in Winterbourne, creating a yeofolk Reeve of Boar's Hollow to buy Bourse materials. The second was a Three Fayres ministry at Brightway, Oldheart and Weaving, creating a Reeve of the Three Fayres who would keep merchants safe and buy goods. The third was the Field of Silver Fishes at Laroc, which must be ceded to the eternal Rhianos and would allow Summer Quests. The fourth was a refurbishment of the Laroc tourney grounds as a great work. None had been built. Each would remain available until the end of the Summer Solstice 385YE.

n.Dawn: Dawn's yeofolk and noble houses were offered new reeve titles, fayres, a Rhianos-linked folly for adventuring military units and fleets, and a refurbished tourney ground that would make upgrading Dawnish military units cheaper for a year.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to Spiral Castle, a Dawnish house seat in Weirwater, rather than to the Grendel-held territory of Spiral.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is named as one of the prosperous lands reachable by the Blood Red Roads, and as a source of travelling merchants for the proposed fayres.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr is listed among the nations whose merchants could reach the proposed Astolat fayres via the Blood Red Roads.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: League merchants are expected to visit the proposed fayres, and Temeschwar and Holberg are linked to Astolat by the Blood Red Roads.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is named as a trading partner reachable by the Blood Red Roads, and Varushkans appear among the guests in the opening story.

t.Astolat: Astolat, described as perhaps Dawn's richest and most peaceful territory, was the focus of all four proposed commissions: two fayre ministries, a folly at Laroc and a great work that would add a share of 743 rings each season to every business in the territory.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story, knights return from Brocéliande with Wisdom pilgrims.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: one branch of the Blood Red Roads runs through the Castle of Thorns to connect Astolat with Casinea.
