t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the northern branch of the Blood Red Roads runs through Weaving and Semmerholm to Holberg city.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Red Roads pass through Semmerholm, and its yeofolk had earlier proposed market-fayres at Applefell or Lacre, which failed to win support.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only as Spiral Castle, a de Cassilon seat in Weirwater, not as this territory.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the Blood Red Roads link Astolat to Temeschwar, whose prosperity the Boar's Hollow market-fayre hopes to draw upon.
t.Weirwater: The de Cassilons of Spiral Castle in Weirwater pledged to patron a grand tourney if the Laroc grounds were refurbished, letting their Castellan upgrade up to a dozen Dawnish military units to rank 2.

r.Astolat/Grovesyard: A monthly fayre was proposed at Brightway in Grovesyard, selling herbs and potions, as one of the Three Fayres.
r.Astolat/The Chase: Laroc in The Chase would host both the proposed Field of Silver Fishes, ceded to Rhianos, and the refurbished tourney grounds great work.
r.Astolat/Winterbourne: Winterbourne would gain the proposed Boar's Hollow market-fayre for Bourse materials and the Weaving fayre, which would sell raw materials at the crossroads of the Blood Red Roads.
r.Astolat/Withy: A fayre was proposed at Oldheart in Withy, selling enchanted rods and mage armour, as one of the Three Fayres.
r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named. The page only notes that the Blood Red Roads pass through Semmerholm.

Grown from the revolution seed.d: Rachensgrab lies in the Tears of the Moon archipelago, more than three weeks' sail north of Volkavaar across the Sea of Steel. Magistrate Abraham found that Empress Deanne's 316YE declaration of war on the slavers had never been revoked, so the attack would be lawful. Sumaah could spare no ships, and the Commonwealth offered only a few ships and a haven for freed slaves. The General Assembly could appoint an admiral to lead the raid. The outcome depended on the strength committed, ranging from scattering ships to razing the city and looting the treasury. No one would pay for the raid unless the guerdon was applied, and the opportunity would pass if it was not taken that season.

n.Druj: The Druj were named as possible trading partners of the Slave Lords. If the Sacrificial Tower were destroyed, the slavers' ships would not dare sail as far as the Bay of Catazar for a generation, cutting the Druj off from new slaves.
n.Grendel: The Slave Lords were said to visit Dubhtraig frequently. A successful assault on the Sacrificial Tower would deny the Grendel access to new slaves for a generation.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Marchers' and Winterfolk's earlier raid on Jotun-held Skallahn was cited as the precedent for appointing a leader for a raid.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: one of the codebreakers began on the stages of Sarvos, and the silk-clad slavers were said to dress in a way a League bravo would envy.

t.Bay of Catazar: If the Sacrificial Tower were destroyed, the Slave Lords' ships would stop sailing as far as the Bay of Catazar for a generation, ending the supply of slaves to the Grendel and Druj there.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the codebreaker Senzio was said to have started out on the cheap stages of Sarvos.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the Marchers' and Winterfolk's raid on Skallahn was cited as the model for appointing someone to lead the assault.

Hopeless as a feather.d: Sadogua will parley in the Hall of Worlds. He will restore three expired boons and reclaim the rest, wants to hear from unhappy Navarri magicians, and will hold a contest to choose the Scholar in the Well. Callidus will open a spirit market run under T'ganyan Auction Rules, with access by ticket. Irra Harah will meet Elienne of Dawn through a Sentinel Gate conjunction to Halver's Dip to discuss Sarangrave and the Barrens, and wants the Hewn Hare returned. Meraud asks for 250 crystal mana to help Suranni magicians flee and to fund a Hand of Dumon breakout from Axiom Prison. Wise Rangara warned that contacting the Silent Witness is extremely unwise. Sinokenon's myrmidons helped the Tsark against Grendel and Axou invaders.

n.Dawn: Elienne of Dawn has been invited to parley with Irra Harah at Halver's Dip, and the Dawnish Archmage of Spring, Ser Fabienne De Miel, may come along without counting against Elienne's two companions.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but helping the people of Sarangrave, which they hold, is the main topic Irra Harah wants to discuss.
n.Grendel: Grendel invaders of the Mountains of the Moon faced Sinokenon's myrmidons, sent to help the Tsark defend their homes. Grendel collectors are also invited to bid separately at Callidus' spirit market.
n.Highguard: Exarch Luke of Highguard, Archmage of Summer, will host Meraud's parley. Ahzrukhal of Highguard holds a seat in Sadogua's contest for Scholar in the Well.
n.Imperial Orcs: Irra Harah complains that the Imperial Orcs were sent the Hewn Hare at the Winter Solstice but did not use it as intended, and wants it returned.
n.Navarr: Sadogua wishes to hear the grievances of Navarri magicians who are unhappy with him, and asks Brat Umbral Path to encourage Morwenna Winterbuilt to attend his parley.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Meraud proposes that some of the requested mana help independent Suranni covens flee across the border into Segura.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Sentinel Gate conjunction for Irra Harah's parley leads to Halver's Dip, a Marcher village in Stock March.
n.Urizen: Urizeni archmages Elyssiathain (Night) and Ematius (Winter) are tied to Sadogua's parley and the Silent Witness meeting respectively, and Spyridonakes of Urizen holds a seat in the Scholar in the Well contest.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: a civil servant recalls dreading Varushka's dark forests, and Sadogua's herald suggests asking the Circle of Zulgan-Tash about the Scholar in the Well.
n.Wintermark: Bærywyn of the Sussivari holds a seat in Sadogua's Scholar in the Well contest, and the Sussivari are named as a source of advice about the role.

t.Bay of Catazar: Meraud says he cannot grant the Summer Archmage's request to split the Bay of Catazar and make a walkway for fleeing Suranni wizards.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the civil servant Jorgen recalls visiting Miekarova and vowing never to go near its forests.
t.Mountains of the Moon: After a warning from the Archmage of Day, Sinokenon sent myrmidons to help the Tsark defend their homes against Grendel and Axou invaders. The Tsark elders have been told the warning came from the Empire.
t.Sarangrave: Helping the people of Sarangrave is to be the main subject of Irra Harah's parley with Elienne of Dawn.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Meraud's proposal would use some of the mana to help Suranni covens escape across the border into Segura.
t.Upwold: The Civil Service identified a Sentinel Gate conjunction to Halver's Dip in Upwold, open for half an hour from 18:30 on Saturday, for Irra Harah's parley.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Jorgen recalls Volodmartz's forests as places he vowed never to approach.

r.Upwold/Stock March: Halver's Dip, a village in Stock March, is the destination of the Sentinel Gate conjunction where Elienne's party must find Irra Harah's friends to hold the parley.

Improve Syrene's Wisdom.d: Proposed by the senator for Casinea and seconded by the senator for Kallavesa, the motion commissioned new pumps for Syrene's Wisdom to improve ilium returns and make conditions safer for miners. The work cost 10 wains of mithril, 10 wains of weirwood and 40 crowns in labour, and takes three months to build. Until it is completed, the mine produces only 4 rings of ilium each season. After the Autumn Equinox, Solomon provided the mithril, the weirwood and 5 thrones. Once complete, the mine's ilium output rises by 2 rings each season, access to silver and other precious metals brings new prosperity to the nearby town, and the new system copes better with flooding, greatly reducing the risk of deaths in the mines.

n.Highguard: Casinea's Highborn senator proposed the motion, and once the work is complete it will make one of the nation's ilium mines more productive and much safer for the miners who work it.

t.Casinea: Syrene's Wisdom in Casinea is to receive modernised pumps; it yields only 4 rings of ilium a season until the work is done, after which output rises by 2 rings, the nearby town gains new prosperity from silver and other precious metals, and the danger of deadly flooding is greatly reduced.

Into tired shadow.d: After three seasons of Highborn crusading storm, backed by liao sent from congregations across the Empire, Imperial armies outmanoeuvred and encircled the Druj in Zenith. Two mandates offered to focus Highborn zeal on the attack. One would impose a two-rank penalty for a season on Highborn military units not supporting the Zenith armies. The other would raise casualties inflicted by Highborn armies fighting the Druj by a fifth for a year, while penalising Highborn armies fighting elsewhere. A competing mandate would have armies hunt down tortured souls, black wraiths and Winter spirits instead. That would cost ten percent fewer casualties and require a Highborn army to stay in Zenith, but would stop Zenith gaining the terrorised quality.

n.Druj: Their six armies in Zenith, thrown into disarray by Karvor Eyepeel's death, were encircled and attempting to flee. Highguard was weighing mandates meant to destroy them, or even carry the war to their heartland.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly faced a choice between mandates. It could pour its zeal into annihilating the Druj, at a heavy cost in Highborn lives and penalties for units or armies that stood aside, or it could purge the Druj's legacy from Zenith instead.
n.Urizen: The Urizeni people of Zenith, labouring under Druj tyranny, faced the prospect that tortured souls, restless dead and miasma could leave their territory permanently terrorised unless Highguard acted.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is not named directly; the page refers only to the Druj's earlier rule of Ossium, which Varushka held at the time.

t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Druj's terror tactics in Zenith are compared to how they ruled Ossium.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: named as a place where Highborn armies could fight the Druj and still benefit from the second Death to the Druj mandate.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: named as a place where Highborn armies could fight the Druj and still benefit from the second Death to the Druj mandate.
t.Zenith: Six Druj armies were trapped and preparing to flee. Without the Shadows of War mandate, the territory would become terrorised, impeding armies and raising commission labour costs by two-fifths.

r.Zenith/Proceris: Mentioned in passing: the Druj armies in Zenith are said to be reinforced by the terrors they unleashed in Proceris.

Let that be your last battlefield.d: The Free Folk spent their wages on offerings and on hand-written pamphlets of ancestor stories. Their greatest concentration was around Caer Faucon in Astolat, where a scarecrow-like effigy at the House of the Proffered Hand became a site of worship said to bear an unusual aura. None had taken citizenship. Adopting the phrase 'The Empire will have All of Us or None of Us', they were saving to make their case to each nation. Priests across the Empire disagreed. The page set out three paths for the General Assembly: accept their beliefs, forbid their public practice, or expel them. It warned that inaction would see the situation deteriorate.

n.Dawn: Dawn gave the Free Folk their first welcome as distant kin. They gathered most heavily around Caer Faucon, helping Dawnish yeofolk with the harvest and visiting their effigy at the House of the Proffered Hand, though they have not settled there as citizens.
n.Highguard: Highborn wayfarers of Shimi's Orchard Chapter examined the Free Folk's paragons and exemplars and found oddities but nothing overtly dangerous. Esau of Shimi's Orchard argued they should be treated no differently from Sumaah figures.
n.Navarr: Some Navarr guides argued that the Free Folk have a place in the Great Dance without changing themselves. They held that it is the Empire's responsibility to help them reach that home, even if it lies outside the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk know most about Dawn and the Brass Coast, and have earlier worked gutting the catch in Siroc.
n.The League: Bishop Jago Heshel di Temeschwar condemned the Free Folk's 'Divine Family' as incompatible with the Doctrines of the Way and likened it to the Yaelian Schism. He demanded that the General Assembly act.
n.The Marches: The Free Folk worked Marcher harvests and gave pamphlets to travellers passing through the Marches, and they adopted a Marcher saying as 'All of Us or None of Us'. Marcher friars urged priests to remember the Doctrine of the Labyrinth and the example of Kethry.
n.Urizen: Urizeni questors called for reason from the Synod, arguing that an unfinished Way must leave room to examine the limits of doctrine. One Urizen priest noted the precedent for inspirational figures not recognised by the Synod.

t.Astolat: Astolat held the largest concentration of Free Folk, who helped bring in its harvest. A scarecrow-like effigy at the House of the Proffered Hand in Caer Faucon became their weekly place of worship, and access to it has been restricted.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk had earlier worked gutting the catch from Siroc.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk had earlier fixed walls and dug ditches in the Mournwold.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk had earlier tamed the undergrowth in the forests of Highrod.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk helped reap the autumn harvest across Semmerholm.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: it is home to Bishop Jago Heshel's Church of the Golden Orator, whose bishop called for the Synod to act against Free Folk beliefs.

r.Astolat/Coombe: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk effigy is described as a scarecrow that would do little to dissuade the jackdaws of Coombe.
r.Necropolis/Highrod: Mentioned in passing: the Free Folk had earlier worked taming the undergrowth in Highrod's forests.

Light upon the water.d: The storms ended the drought but halved the production of every farm and business and cost every mine a rank. Loss of life was small. Regrow the Land's Heart left extra herbs and eased old grudges. Utterlund and Eastring became marshes, and marsh commissions cost a fifth more labour for at least a year. The Vassa flooded Tassato and damaged the Imperial Mint, revealing hidden flooded chambers, and the rains uncovered ilium in the hills. The Semmerlak washed up curious treasures. The Meade flooded the Marches, angering threshers and reviving the Great Western Canal proposal. True liao was stolen in Madruga, and Syrene's Wisdom gained ilium.

n.Dawn: Dawnish lakeshore lands flooded, Culwich worst of all, where the drowned bells rang in Summer. Troubadours warned of cursed Sedaret, and a proposed mandate would send 50 doses of liao to keep Dawnish folk from the Semmerlak's trinkets.
n.Druj: The Barrens and Druj-held Zenith escaped the rituals' direct effects but still face the higher labour costs on marsh commissions. Sarangrave's Nesustak Forest became swampier near the lake.
n.Highguard: The storm clouds seemed to spread from Casinea, where Regrow the Land's Heart was targeted. The Silver Chalice shielded Syrene, which gave the order two vials of Pool of Syrene water, and Syrene's Wisdom stays flooded but gains a ring of ilium each season.
n.Jotun: Jotun-held Bregasland and Liathaven were spared the magical storms but still face the fifth-higher labour cost on marsh commissions, as floodwater ignored borders.
n.Navarr: The Feverwater rose and turned Eastring in Therunin into a marsh, while the Navarr and Great Forest Orcs struggled to limit the damage elsewhere in the territory.
n.The Brass Coast: A flooded Civil Service vault in Madruga was emptied in haste and a dose of true liao was stolen. The Great Grasses dried out oddly fast, and there are worries about the Scorrero River.
n.The League: The Vassa flooded Tassato despite the Assembly's warning, damaging the Imperial Mint and leaving businesses penalised until repairs are paid for. New ilium was found in the hills, Holberg's Utterlund became a marsh, and Sarvos's precautions largely protected it.
n.The Marches: The Meade burst its banks across Mitwold, Upwold and the Mournwold, and threshers grew angry at the Empire cursing its own people. They want the Assembly to name the casters, and the Great Western Canal has been proposed.
n.Urizen: Zenith, shared with the Druj, was outside the rituals' direct reach but faces higher marsh labour costs, and the Lustri forests became swampier near the lake.
n.Varushka: Floods struck Varushkan settlements on the Semmerlak, including the vales of Bittershore. Wise ones warned that the lake's treasures may be Dho'uala's lures, and a proposed mandate would send 25 doses of liao to discourage Varushkans from taking them.

t.Bregasland: Not Imperial at the time, Bregasland escaped the direct storms, but the higher labour cost on marsh commissions still applies there.
t.Brocéliande: Brocéliande only had to endure the drought, but floodwater ignored borders and marsh commissions there now cost a fifth more labour.
t.Casinea: The storm clouds seemed to spread out from Casinea's regio. In Syrene the Silver Chalice protected the people, though homes were lost and Syrene's Wisdom remains flooded, with higher upkeep but an extra ring of ilium each season.
t.Holberg: Utterlund became a marsh and the Great Pits of Ennerlund flooded badly. Sand Fisher orcs helped shore up defences to protect the city, but Holberg gains no Semmerlak bounty as the city does not border the lake.
t.Karov: Karov's shores of the Semmerlak flooded, and its businesses stand to gain 2 crowns and two random ingots of rare metal at the Winter Solstice unless a Varushkan mandate turns people away from the lake's treasures.
t.Karsk: As a territory bordering the Semmerlak, Karsk suffered flooding, and its businesses may share in the lake's Winter Solstice bounty unless a Varushkan mandate is upheld.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven was spared the magical storms but is among the territories where marsh commissions now carry a fifth more labour cost.
t.Madruga: A Madruga vault holding Civil Service cargo for Anvil flooded, and a dose of true liao was stolen in the confusion. The Great Grasses dried out unnaturally quickly afterwards.
t.Mitwold: The Meade flooded parts of Mitwold, ruining crops. The proposed Great Western Canal would boost its businesses and farms and help prevent future floods.
t.Mournwold: The Meade flooded parts of the Mourn. The Great Western Canal would link Meade to Sarcombe and enrich its businesses and mines, and the Mournwold thralls offer half the labour cost if it is commissioned before the end of the Spring Equinox 385YE.
t.Ossium: The vales along Bittershore flooded. Ossium's businesses may gain the Semmerlak bounty, but its under-developed areas now also face the higher marsh labour costs.
t.Sarangrave: The Nesustak Forest weathered the storm better than most but became significantly swampier where it borders the lake.
t.Sarvos: Precautions Sarvos had taken since Skathe's curse helped the city endure the storms with minimal lasting damage.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm's lakeshore suffered flooding, and its businesses may gain 2 crowns and two random rare-metal ingots from the Semmerlak's flotsam unless a Dawnish mandate is upheld.
t.Tassato: The Vassa broke its banks and flooded Tassato, damaging the Imperial Mint and leaving businesses at a rank penalty until the Senate pays 50 Thrones or a year passes. Hidden chambers were found beneath the Mint and ilium in the northern hills.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Gemma Stewart says missing mining infrastructure for the new Tassatan ilium seat could be sourced from Holberg or Temeschwar.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens were outside the rituals' direct effects, but the higher labour cost for marsh commissions applies there too.
t.The Semmerlak: The lake rose dramatically, and as it receded it left junk and strange treasures that drew scavengers. Some fear these are Dho'uala's lures or relics of drowned Sedaret.
t.Therunin: The rising Feverwater turned Eastring into a marsh, while the Navarr and Great Forest Orcs worked hard to contain the damage across the rest of Therunin.
t.Upwold: The Meade flooded parts of Upwold. An alder suggested the canal might make up for wealth lost when Moonwater Hall was abrogated.
t.Weirwater: Culwich suffered the worst of the Semmerlak flooding, and its drowned bells were heard in Summer as an ill omen. Weirwater's businesses may share the lake's bounty, which some link to the territory's strange dreams.
t.Zenith: Zenith escaped the direct effects of the rituals, but marsh commissions there now cost a fifth more labour and the Lustri forests became swampier near the lake.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund saw some of their worst flooding since reverting to the Morass, though the Bourse seat weathered it without permanent damage.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: Utterlund permanently gained the marsh quality alongside its forest, so commissions there cost a fifth more labour for at least a year.
r.Karov/Malimorzi: As part of Karov's Semmerlak shore, Malimorzi shared in the lakeside flooding, which affected settlements such as Korotny and forced people onto higher ground.
r.Ossium/Bittershore: Flooding in the vales along Bittershore was less severe than at Culwich but still drove people to upper storeys and higher ground.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The Nesustak Forest endured the storm better than most places but grew significantly more swampy where it meets the lake.
r.Semmerholm/Lacuve: Lacuve's stretch of the Semmerlak shore shared in the lakeside flooding, which affected settlements such as Lacre and left many people seeking higher ground.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Mestra was flooded, and ilium washed out of old mines in the hills above it could become a Bourse seat yielding 6 rings a season: 75 Thrones with the guilds' help if made a League position, or 250 Thrones otherwise.
r.Therunin/Eastring: The rising Feverwater gave Eastring the marsh quality, making commissions there costlier to build.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The forests of Lustri endured the storm relatively well but became significantly swampier where they border the lake.

Mosaic.d: More than eighty Imperial warbands and twice that many fleets joined the Sumaah and Commonwealth at Xeier before striking Chalonsio, a rich slaving and shipbuilding city in the satrapy of Chanteolleth. The harbour and defences fell quickly. Raiders broke the slave markets of the Chain District and freed captives, assaulted the Grand Temple during a convocation of the God of Chains' priesthood and slew its leaders, then besieged the Sapphire Keep. They executed Patrio Sebastian Ceruleo, looted the vaults and fired the palace, docks and shipyards. The Asavean slave trade is crippled for years. Participants gained crowns, materials, herbs and mithril. Recovered intelligence on the slaving fleet of the Noble Lady of the Sea creates an opportunity to strike its stronghold.

n.Dawn: Dawnish nobles and their forces, including Destan Weaver of house DeRondell and Solene d'Alba, sailed with the armada and shared in the spoils of Chalonsio.
n.Highguard: A sizeable Highborn contingent, among them Caleb of the Cenotaph and Lazarus of the Necropolis, fought in the raid. Their units and fleets claimed a share of the plunder and the chance of a righteous epiphany.
n.Imperial Orcs: Dozens of orc citizens' units took part, including many of the Irontide and Bloodcrow. Rather than an epiphany, orcs who fought may have heard an ancestor urging them to kill the slavers and the priests of the God of Chains, and may go on hearing that voice clearly.
n.Navarr: A large number of Navarr citizens sent their warbands and fleets with the Liberty Pact armada and gained a share of the treasure, herbs and mithril taken from the city.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn sent by far the largest contingent of named participants to the raid. Their fleets and units shared in the wealth seized from the Chain District, the temple and the Ceruleo vaults.
n.The League: League citizens from Holberg, Tassato, Catazar, Sarvos and Temeschwar joined the raid, and their forces shared in the plunder of Chalonsio.
n.The Marches: Only two Marcher citizens, Tomothy Crowle and William Delerougemont, are listed as supporting the raid. Their forces shared in the rewards.
n.Urizen: Urizeni citizens, including Laurentius Julianus Netherwatch and Romulus of the Scarlet Guard, committed their forces to the raid and shared its spoils.
n.Varushka: Varushkan citizens such as Vuk the Wolfeater and Yulia Kasimirova Voronov sent forces to Chalonsio and received a share of the plunder.
n.Wintermark: A small Wintermark contingent, including Leif Arnbjorn and Sven Cuttler, took part in the raid and shared in its rewards.

t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: one Highborn participant in the raid is named Lazarus of the Necropolis.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: several League participants in the raid bear the Temeschwar name, such as Danica Lidija van Temeschwar.

Never be found at home.d: Imperial fleets destroyed the bridges, watchtowers and garrisons of the Kongegőr, which links Skallahn and Hordalant and normally blocks large naval forces leaving the Gullet. The Jotun were already working on repairs, so the chance lasted only one season. A Senate motion costing 50 thrones would have the civil service supply cartographers to captains willing to commit fleets. The more fleets that joined, the more the Empire would learn: names of territories, a route south to Faraden, details of Narkyst and Kalsea and their monarchs, and the icy waters of Tsirku. A legendary passage to Ultima Thule might also be found. Any new ports reached could raise tax revenues in the territories bordering the Gullet.

n.Jotun: The Imperial raid tore down a thousand years of Jotun infrastructure on the Kongegőr, and the Jotun were hurrying to rebuild it. An expedition could chart the coasts of Narkyst and Kalsea and perhaps learn about King Gudmundur Arason and Queen Yrsa Jansdóttir.
n.The Marches: Only Marcher and Wintermark fleets could join the expedition at full strength. Marcher merchants are among the few who have ever slipped past the Jotun into the Sea of Snow, and new ports could boost Mitwold's tax revenues.
n.Thule: In the accompanying story the Thule are named as a people wary of the sea. A large enough armada might find the fabled passage to Ultima Thule and open a port with the northern orcs.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark captains could commit fleets at full strength, and some Wintermark merchants have already braved the Sea of Snow. New ports could raise tax revenues in Kallavesa.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland borders the Gullet and could gain tax revenue from new ports, but only once it is back under Imperial control rather than Jotun rule.
t.Hordalant: Hordalant is joined to Skallahn by the damaged Kongegőr, and expedition fleets would turn south past its already well-mapped coast to chart what lies beyond.
t.Kallavesa: If the expedition opened new ports in Faraden or Nithoggir, merchants would find new business opportunities and Kallavesa's tax revenues would rise.
t.Mitwold: As a territory bordering the Gullet, Mitwold would see increased tax revenues if new ports were opened through the expedition.
t.Sea of Snow: With the Kongegőr broken, large Imperial fleets could for once enter the Sea of Snow to map its little-known coastline and the territories around it.
t.Skallahn: Last season's Imperial raid on Skallahn destroyed the Kongegőr defences, and expedition fleets could sail quickly past its well-mapped shore on their way north.
t.Tsirku: A big enough armada could reach the ice-choked waters of Tsirku, a region almost unknown and said to hide frozen-buried jungles and man-eating sea monsters.

Of earth and sky.d: After the Summer Solstice the Lasambrians and their yegarra allies tore up roads and bridges, cutting Braydon's Jasse off from Serra Briante and Serra Damata, then massed on Jade Range to take Fort Braydon. The Black Thorns, Quiet Step, Isaella's Dance, Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs, aided by the fort's garrison, struck instead. The Navarr pursued slaughter under a ravens-haunted mist that fed bloodlust, while the Freeborn raided supplies. Skjalderborn reinforcements failed to stop the rout at Nestor's Bounty. The ritual Shroud of Fog and Ravens has been rendered unworkable by the Lock's conjunction. The Empire could fight at Rojota over the fate of the wounded orcs, and could use a conjunction to Talaeiros to rescue the abducted quarry-woman Catalina.

n.Jotun: The Lasambrian Escuta, Hierro and Corazón were routed from Jade Range into Gambit with heavy losses despite Summer elves and Skjalderborn reinforcements. Up to a thousand of their wounded trapped in Rojota, and a thousand more across Gambit, could be rescued, ransomed, released or killed depending on the battle.
n.Navarr: All three Navarr armies, including the newly mustered Isaella's Dance, led a merciless campaign of slaughter in Kahraman. Two were under a fog-and-ravens enchantment that magnified bloodlust and has now failed. Arhallogen has offered vague aid to the Navarr generals.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire of the South and Red Wind Corsairs helped liberate Jade Range and raided Lasambrian supplies and plunder, alongside Fort Braydon's garrison. The Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills has been asked to rescue Catalina i Burna i Riqueza of the Damatian Cliffs.
n.The Marches: The Mournwolder renegade Steven of Sarcombe and his yegarra bill block fought for the Jotun and are leading the push to rescue the wounded at Rojota. Killing him would break his force.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's habit of avoiding needless bloodshed against the Jotun is cited as the model for letting the wounded Lasambrians withdraw.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: news of Mathilda's sweeping victory in Bregasland has raised the spirits of Steven of Sarcombe's yegarra.
t.Kahraman: Imperial armies reclaimed Jade Range and are a third of the way to expelling the Lasambrians. The wrecked roads still isolate Braydon's Jasse, Serra Briante and Serra Damata from one another until they can be repaired.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the yegarra fighting for the Lasambrians are humans raised under Jotun rule in the Mourn, and the Jotun's hostility is traced back to the Mournwold's devastation.
t.Reinos: Corazón raiders are fleeing towards Reinos with plunder and the captive Catalina. They apparently plan to force her to open a white granite quarry on small deposits there.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Fort Braydon was the Lasambrian target. Its garrison, reinforced by brass constructs from Shikal, sallied out to join the counter-attack, but the broken roads mean the fort now defends only its own region.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Lasambrians were driven back into Gambit and are camped at the edge of the Sand Woods, with wounded trapped in Rojota and scattered across the region. A conjunction to Talaeiros offers a chance to ambush Catalina's captors.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Lasambrians massed on the drought-wilted Jade Range, then were broken at Nestor's Bounty and swept from the region, which the Empire has reclaimed.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Collapsed roads and bridges cut Serra Briante off from Braydon's Jasse and Serra Damata, threatening access to the Great Mine of Briante and limiting the reach of local fortifications.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: Serra Damata was isolated by the sabotage, and Corazón raiders abducted Catalina i Burna i Riqueza, the legendary head quarry-woman of the Damatian Cliffs, a bitter blow to the quarry.

Secure Wunderkind Woods.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Sarvos, the motion took up the opportunity set out in the Dear green space Wind of Fortune. It let the Rebeshi Players of Holberg cultivate the Blood Orchard in Holmauer Park, formerly Wunderkind Woods, and harvest both vis and wood from its twisted trees. It was to be funded by the Looking Glass, cost 32 crowns and take three months; Flávio Capra Gláucio van Holberg provided 4 thrones after the Autumn Equinox. The new title, Tender of the Blood Orchard, is appointed annually by unanimous decision of the League's senators. It liaises with the Players and may buy the valuable Winter vis, with access to a ministry producing Winter vis and ritual staves.

n.The League: The League gained a new Imperial title, the Tender of the Blood Orchard, appointed by its senators, giving a League citizen access to Winter vis and ritual staves from Holberg's Rebeshi Players.

t.Holberg: Holberg's Rebeshi Players were recognised as Guardians of the Wood and allowed to cultivate the Blood Orchard within the city.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer Park, formerly Wunderkind Woods, became the site of the Blood Orchard, whose twisted trees the Rebeshi Players may now harvest for vis and wood.

Summer tree.d: Over thirty thousand orcs and their human allies overran The Rushes and Gravenmarch. Mathilda Fisher planted her leaping-fish standard at Graven and set up her court at Fisher's Rock, where a wooden town of stilt-houses is rising. Many Bregas stayed as thralls, giving the bare minimum of cooperation. The Strong Reeds, supported by House Greywater, lay low and raided Jotun supplies. Fisher's cousin Bron claimed the Keeper of the Dour Fens's mana, and the Imperial Breadbasket now feeds Jotun armies. Fisher planned to send a delegation to Anvil to seek Bregasland's neutrality. A Sentinel Gate conjunction to Jayne's Top Copse offered heroes a chance to destroy a Jotun stockade.

n.Jotun: Jotun armies, including the Mandowla's Roar, now hold all of Bregasland and claim the Imperial Breadbasket's bounty, but their supply lines and food stores suffer constant raids. They have built no fortifications, apparently because moving white granite through the rebel-held marshes is so hard.
n.The Marches: Marchers lost the whole of Bregasland. Many Bregas fled, while those who stayed live as surly, minimally cooperative thralls. The Marcher army the Strong Reeds remains hidden in the marshes, harrying the occupiers alongside House Greywater.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the new buildings at Fisher's Rock are likened to Kallavesi stilt-houses rather than traditional Marcher dwellings.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland fell entirely under Jotun and Fisher control, with Mathilda Fisher as its new steward. Resistance by the Strong Reeds and House Greywater continues, and Fisher hopes to have the territory recognised as a neutral free state between the Jotun and the Marches.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is one of the places Bregas fled to as their marshes fell.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium is not referred to on this page; the only Varushkan link is a comparison of Fisher's Rock's buildings to Kallavesi stilt-houses.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Gravenmarch fell to the Jotun, and Mathilda Fisher planted her battle standard in Graven's town square. Her cousin Bron now styles himself Keeper and claims the crystal mana from beneath Graven Rock.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: House Greywater's harassment gives the Grey Fens allied insurgents, so it counts as a beach head for the Empire. A conjunction to Jayne's Top Copse there offered heroes the chance to destroy a Mandowla's Roar stockade.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: Mathilda Fisher has firmly established her court at Fisher's Rock in the North Fens, where a wooden town of stilt-houses is being built around the rock. It is the only significant construction in the marshes.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: The Rushes fell quickly to the Jotun force of more than thirty thousand orcs and their human allies.

The bones of what you believe.d: The Great Library at Mourning Hollow could be commissioned as a folly, available until the end of the Winter Solstice 384YE: 50 wains of white granite, 40 of weirwood, 30 of mithril and 240 crowns, taking a year. Two further years of study would follow. Mandates open to the League, Highguard and the General Assembly, and the Imperial Archivist's offer of historical research, could shorten that study or divert Bourse materials to the build. A Miaren brand proposed the Hall of the Seven, which would create the Spear of the Seven title and a ruin-exploring action. Minions of Cintra Blackstaff seized two vates, and a conjunction to Whisperwood offered a rescue attempt.

n.Dawn: Dawnish knights questing into the heart of Brocéliande inspired Navarr thorns and the Hall of the Seven proposal, and Navarr formally thanked Bertrand of House Sepulchre for building Greenwood Manor as a staging point for those knights.
n.Druj: Having fled to Sarangrave after reverses in Zenith, the ghulai Cintra Blackstaff had minions capture and interrogate two Navarr vates, apparently desperate to learn more about the vallorn.
n.Highguard: The Highborn assembly could mandate archivists and grey pilgrims to copy their vallorn lore, cutting the research by three months. A separate mandate could share statements of principle with the Navarr assembly for a year, though a General Assembly mandate would cut the Cinderpath Exchange's output.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, though the opening poem speaks of orcs squabbling on the outskirts of Liathaven, whose ruins Navarr explorers might one day reach.
n.Navarr: The Navarr could gather their scattered lore, guarded since Nicovar burned the libraries, into an expanded Great Library that promises a way to destroy the vallorn. They were also offered the Hall of the Seven, the Spear of the Seven title and the Temple of the Waking Dream, while two of their vates were held by the Druj.
n.The League: Building on Alessi di Trivento's statement, the League assembly could urge its scholars to search their libraries for vallorn and Navarr lore, cutting the research by three months. League donations and the Towerjacks might also help with construction.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the opening poem describes the vallorn heart Emrys in Sküld as a prisoner of the Thule, smothered by winter.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: if a General Assembly mandate passed with a greater majority, the Iron Roundtower and the Docks at Korotny would lose part of their output to the library effort.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Kauppahall would lose its top two ranks of production if the General Assembly mandate supporting the library were enacted.

t.Brocéliande: Dawnish knights were exploring the heart of Brocéliande, the battlefield where the Navarr were fighting. Its ruins were among the harder-to-reach sites that the proposed Explore the ruins of Terunael action would cover.
t.Hercynia: The Great Library of Hacynian at Mourning Hollow could be rebuilt as an Empire-wide centre of Navarr history and vallorn study. Hercynia's accessible ruins would also be open to Navarr explorers if the Hall of the Seven were built.
t.Holberg: The recent consecration in Holberg inspired its academics to seek novel solutions to the Empire's problems, and the League assembly urged Holberg's citizens to visit the Great Library to help tackle the vallorn.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven's vallorn was described as wounded but cut off from the trods. The Navarr pointedly rejected closer ties with its Feni, and its ruins were counted among the harder-to-reach sites for explorers.
t.Miaren: Miaren was proposed as the site of the Hall of the Seven. Enthusiasm also grew for turning Seren into the City of Dreams, awaiting a Senate commission for the Temple of the Waking Dream.
t.Otkodov: The Terunael ruins in Otkodov, outside Imperial borders, would be among those Navarr military units could explore if the Hall of the Seven were built.
t.Sarangrave: Cintra Blackstaff fled to Sarangrave with a stolen vallorn ritual text, and her minions held two captured vates there. Its ruins would also be open to Navarr explorers via the Hall of the Seven.
t.Therunin: Therunin's ruins were among the relatively accessible sites for the proposed exploration action. Prognosticators had expected Cintra Blackstaff to flee here, though she went to Sarangrave instead.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: a sudden reversal of Druj fortunes in Zenith drove Cintra Blackstaff east, and Highguard's armies were said to be focused on the fight there.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Mentioned in passing: the opening poem laments that the chance to take Dark Ranging was slipping through Navarr fingers.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: the poem names the forests of Terunael as the heart of hearts and the battlefield where the Navarr were then fighting.
r.Miaren/Serenael: The proposed Hall of the Seven would be built in the City of Seren in Serenael, which the Navarr had also voted to make the City of Dreams.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: the poem says the vallorn heart Emrys on Sküld's cold plains has been bound with oaths and will fall in time.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: the poem refers to the fallen city of Béantal Dol as lying beyond the trods, too far to reach for now.
r.Sarangrave/Whisperwood: A conjunction to Karliss in Whisperwood led to the Druj camp holding the captured vates, and the Dredgemaster of the Feverwater was asked to arrange a rescue.

The city asleep.d: Drawn by Imperial daring, Rhianos proposed placing the ancient, nearly exhausted cauldron at the Broch in Black Boughs. Its onion soup grants protection from venom, sickness and the miasma. Brocéliande's vallorn remains weakened by Wither the Seed. Military units, not armies, could join an expedition into the forest in place of normal production, earning forest resources, herbs, weirwood, ilium and relics. Greater strength reaches deeper: securing northern Brocéliande, looting the abandoned Heirs of Terunael base, the vallorn gardens, a hidden weirwood grove, the walls of Terunael and finally the vallorn heart itself. Navarr, Highborn and Dawnish mandates and choices, and Great Forest Orc aid, could swell the effort.

n.Dawn: Rhianos' heralds came to Dawn, and Dawnish knights who joined the expedition were offered a one-rank bonus to strength and rewards. Alternatively they could quest independently from the newly completed Greenwood Market and Manor.
n.Druj: If the expedition gathered enough strength, the remaining Druj would be cleared out of northern Brocéliande, with treasures seized from them.
n.Highguard: Heralds visited Highguard, and the Highborn Assembly could revive the Blade of the Pilgrims for a final season. Congregations would sacrifice liao and Synod votes to add 1,000 or 2,000 strength, with reduced cost if Hazelelponi of the Shattered Tower enacted it.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's raid on Skallahn is cited, and the vallorn of Liathaven serves as a point of comparison.
n.Navarr: The Navarr hosted the heralds at the Broch and prepared for many visitors. Their National Assembly could urge every thorn to join, with Navarr units taking any other action penalised until Winter.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: farmers in Mournwold are among those reporting eerie Spring-touched plants where the vallorn has reached.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat farmers have spoken of eerie plants steeped in Spring magic growing where the vallorn has touched.
t.Brocéliande: The whole adventure takes place in Brocéliande, the largest vallorn near the Empire. Success could secure the north of the forest, uncover the Heirs' base and penetrate ruined Terunael.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea farmers have reported strange Spring-steeped plants growing where the vallorn has touched.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn is dwarfed by Brocéliande's, and the weirwood grove found there is compared to the hoped-for sanctuary near Terunael.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the destruction of Miaren some 350 years ago was the last time anyone looked upon a vallorn heart.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold farmers have spoken of eerie vallorn-touched plants.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: listed only in further reading, via a later expedition to Bendol.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial raid on Skallahn was one of the daring deeds that caught Rhianos' attention.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the liberation of the Barrens by independent orcs led the Great Forest Orcs to leave Boar's Dell for the Eaves of Peytaht.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest Orcs of Therunin offered to send the Spears of the Pines, adding 1,000 strength, if invited by Therunin's senator or the Imperial Consul. They would give more help, including extra weirwood, if granted Imperial lore by the Conclave.

r.Brocéliande/Black Boughs: The cauldron was to be placed at the heart of the reinforced Broch in Black Boughs, the starting point for every band joining the adventure.
r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Boar's Dell is free of vallorn, and success could secure its borders against Mallum orcs and link it by safe routes to the Broch. It was once home to the Great Forest Orcs.
r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Mentioned in passing: the earlier opportunity to attack Dark Ranging is noted as no longer available.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Elerael is free of vallorn, and a successful adventure could secure its borders with watches against Mallum orcs and safe routes to the Broch.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: The ruined city of Terunael and its vallorn heart were the ultimate goal. Deep success could breach its walls or even look upon the heart for the first time in centuries.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: a later report from an expedition to Bendol appears in further reading.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs are said to have returned to the Eaves of Peytaht after the Barrens were liberated.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Chief Vallack of the Great Forest Orcs is in the Lower Tarn Valley. A Winged Messenger to him from Therunin's senator or the Consul would send the Spears of the Pines.

The darkest road.d: After Kavor Eyepeel's death, Druj forces in Zenith lost cohesion. The Towerjacks took Iteri and the Citadel Guard raised a citadel in Clypion. Thousands of doses of liao, sent under Aurum of the Nightingale Temple's mandate, anointed Imperial soldiers against the miasma. A Highborn and Dawnish host came through Morrow into Lustri, and the Hounds of Glory lost hundreds to complete the encirclement. Zenith became Imperial again, but the hold is fragile: losing any region loses the territory. The Druj armies remain hale and plan to have the Tainted Basilisk enchant them with Night magic before fleeing. The Glass Labyrinth limits their escape, and conjunctions offer chances to destroy miasma pillars and monsters.

n.Dawn: The Hounds of Glory, bound with Autumn magic and reinforced by eleven thousand soldiers, refused to accept anything short of victory and drove the last orcs from Lustri at the cost of hundreds of knights and yeomen. The Endless Stalker has since been preying on their camps in Lustri.
n.Druj: The Druj lost Zenith. Seven of their armies are trapped in Proceris and Occursion and can only escape at devastating cost, and their generals are gathering at the Glade of Night Enshrouding to be enchanted by the Tainted Basilisk.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the trapped Druj armies cannot easily leave Zenith unless they attack Grendel-held Spiral.
n.Highguard: The Highborn armies inspired the virtuous crusade in both the west and north of Zenith. Nearly a thousand of Kaela's unkillable warriors were sent among the Druj specifically to face Highguard's soldiers.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the trapped Druj armies are compared to the Black Thorns once trapped in Liathaven.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave marched through Therunin, and a Druj escape into Therunin is described as near suicide.
n.The League: Thomas di Holberg, a reformed bravo turned priest, located a lone miasma pillar in Iteri. He has offered the Captain of the Sea Wolves 5 crowns to deal with it and hopes other loyal Holbergers will add to the sum.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave's route ran through Mournwold, and even dour Marchers among the warbands were stirred by Dawn's fire.
n.Urizen: Zenith is an Imperial territory again, and the Citadel Guard raised a citadel and renewed the Glass Labyrinth. Urizeni dreamed of a song, 'The Darkest Road', which strengthened their resolve and sharply reduced the number accepting Kaela's Gift.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus had briefly resupplied in Bastion before returning to Zenith.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Thomas di Holberg's past and the Druj attacks on the city are recounted, and he argues Holberg owes the Empire its help.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the Druj predicament is likened to the Black Thorns once trapped in Liathaven.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky and Seventh Wave circled through Morrow's mountains to join the attack on Lustri.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave's general planned to move through Mournwold on the way round to Lustri.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: tortured souls were first encountered during the Druj invasion of Reikos.
t.Sarangrave: With Lustri taken, the Empire controls the passage to Sarangrave. Druj armies trying to push through to it from Zenith would suffer heavy losses.
t.Spiral: Attacking Spiral is the only way the trapped Druj armies can easily leave Zenith.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Seventh Wave's planned route ran through Therunin, and a Druj break-out there would be tantamount to suicide.
t.Zenith: Zenith returned to Imperial control and can be assigned to a nation, though it has no Bourse resources and will be lost if any region falls. Druj armies, miasma pillars and tortured souls remain within it.

r.Zenith/Clypion: The Empire held Clypion after the summer victory over Kavor Eyepeel, and the Citadel Guard raised a citadel of ice and black stone there as a refuge.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The Druj quickly conceded Iteri to the Towerjacks. A lone miasma pillar has been found at the Pallasian Steps, guarded by Druj and at least three tortured souls.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The northern host smashed through Lustri's Night-magic defences, and the Hounds of Glory claimed the region at great cost, sealing the Druj escape route. Linked miasma pillars at the Spire of Twisting Shadow and the Endless Stalker at the Rift in the Veil remain threats.
r.Zenith/Occursion: Occursion is one of the two regions where the Druj armies are trapped. Their generals are gathering at the Glade of Night Enshrouding for a Night enchantment, the target of the Sunday battle. Further conjunctions target the Field of Celestial Mist pillar and a poison camp near the Tower of the Fall.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Druj refused to yield Proceris, defending it from a Spring-magic fortress amid corrupted waters teeming with carnivorous octopus creatures. Three linked miasma pillars and a marshling at the Plantation of Tall Ferns are conjunction targets.

The long bench.d: Alders-Baart Sarcophans arrived from Crown's Quay with a sack of cursed items to sell. Lord Barien's heralds held court at House Del'Toro with challenge scrolls and invitations to rewardings. Jezda the Harbinger sought Alderei the Fair. Priests questioned the looting during the Chalonsio and Skallahn raids. Marracossans of Trajadoz, Asavean visitors, the Tamazi, Terun-Axou ex-slaves, Kaban traders, a Grendel game-master and Parnau's Hanus Kovac, seeking to settle the idle Pallas Docks, all planned visits. The Wintergard chapter sought help with strange events after the Syrene flood. Conjunctions reached the Ketsov Winter Market, soured by accusations of inhospitality, and Calvos, where visiting Sumaah were behaving strangely.

n.Dawn: Barien's heralds asked Solene d'Alba or another representative of House de Gauvain to confirm a completed challenge, and they hoped for hosts outside Dawn, Wintermark and the Brass Coast.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Ketsov of Karsk are described as a former subject clan of the Druj from Ossium.
n.Grendel: Kayley, a Grendel Master of Ceremonies, brought the Broken Shore game Beggars' Lot to Anvil, running four games on Friday evening with buy-ins of 1 and 10 thrones.
n.Highguard: Members of the Wintergard chapter planned to visit the Highguard camp seeking help, and possibly inquisitors, to investigate reports of people in Syrene's Wisdom linked to the recent flood.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Tamazi, freed orcs of Axos increasingly embracing citizenship as Imperial Orcs, came to Anvil to meet artisans, academics and bankers and learn about Imperial magic.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: priests asked whether the attack on Skallahn was a virtuous response to the Jotun threat or an excuse for plunder.
n.Navarr: Terun-Axou former slaves who had asked the Navarr about their shared history planned to meet past helpers and anyone supporting their fight against the vallorn in Axos at the Navarr noticeboard.
n.The Brass Coast: Barien's heralds held court at House Del'Toro, Asavean 'priests' landed at Siroc, Marracossans of Trajadoz traded with Torres, and sutannir were invited to lift spirits in Calvos.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni spires were among those gathering, and Kayley's game met at the gate between the Urizen and Varushka camps.
n.Varushka: Jezda the Harbinger of the Seers of the Black Gate planned to visit the Varushkan camp to meet Alderei the Fair, and tensions arose around the Ketsov settlers in Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Barien's heralds preferred offers to host them from nations other than Wintermark, Dawn or the Brass Coast.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page; the link is through the discussion of the raid on the Asavean city of Chalonsio and Asavean visitors arriving by sea.
t.Casinea: After a Winter-tainted flood struck Syrene in Syrwatch, the Wintergard chapter sought help investigating strange reports from Syrene's Wisdom mine.
t.Karsk: The Ketsov clan's Winter Market in their new vale was marred by accusations of poor hospitality, and a conjunction let a small group visit.
t.Madruga: Sumaah Präster visiting Calvos for the Festival of Zemress acted strangely, and Marracossans from Trajadoz traded with Torres and travelled towards Anvil.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Sarcophan Alders-Baart visitors were met on the road to Anvil from Crown's Quay.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Ketsov clan, now settled in Karsk, originally came from Ossium.
t.Redoubt: With the Jarm embargo, weirwood stopped flowing through the Pallas Docks in Cargo, and Parnau's Hanus Kovac came to discuss their ownership with the Prime Factor and the Ambassador to Jarm.
t.Semmerholm: Gemma Brightsmith's rewarding ceremony with Barien's heralds was set for the Grove of the Thousand near the Semerstones in Axmure.
t.Skallahn: Priests questioned whether the recent attack on Skallahn was virtuous or mere banditry, and sought those who had sent forces there.

r.Casinea/Syrwatch: The town of Syrene, flooded with Winter-tainted water during the Great Drought, saw unexplained reports of people inside Syrene's Wisdom mine that the Wintergard chapter wanted investigated.
r.Karsk/Lestasny: The Ketsov's results-first attitude divided opinion in Lestasny, and their interrogations and ejections of visitors, often draughir, worsened local attitudes ahead of their Winter Market.
r.Madruga/Torres: A bountiful season saw the Marracossan exiles of Trajadoz surge their trade with neighbouring Torres before seeking wider Imperial ties.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: Barien's heralds were to hold Gemma Brightsmith's rewarding ceremony at the Grove of the Thousand near the Semerstones.

Throw back the echoes.d: The General Assembly's upheld mandate imposed a one-fifth penalty on territory captured by Imperial armies in the Barrens using any order other than break the chains, until the Summer Solstice 385YE. Urizen and Varushkan armies were exempt because it lacked a greater majority. The Dawnish Assembly could pass one of three mandates: defy the rebuke while penalising Dawnish units not supporting the Barrens campaign, or embrace it and raise the penalty to a quarter or three tenths. Jaheris offered monsters to guard Dawnguard in return for a fane. Janon offered triumphant charge to Dawnish armies in return for rededicating Laroc Cathedral. Tharim offered steel-bound knights in return for feasting on Dawn's farms, mana sites and commissions. Sorin offered wolves to House Aurelius through a ritual.

n.Dawn: Dawn's centuries-old ambition to conquer the Barrens faced the Synod's penalty, and its Assembly and enchanters were offered mandates and eternal bargains to press the claim, each at a cost.
n.Druj: The Druj, whose armies were described as trapped in Zenith facing annihilation, held the Barrens and guarded the regio that House Aurelius could use to summon Sorin's wolves against them.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard was noted as having answered Dawn's challenge to take the most regions in the Barrens.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Tharim had previously sent his servants to fight the vallorn alongside the Navarr in return for feasting on their herb gardens and forests.
n.Urizen: Urizen's armies, including the Citadel Guard, were exempt from the Synod's penalty on conquering the Barrens because the mandate lacked a greater majority.
n.Varushka: Varushka explicitly joined Dawn's challenge to help reclaim the Barrens, and its armies were exempt from the Synod's penalty as they reject mandates not passed with a greater majority.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the symbols on Tharim's steel-bound knights were said to be nothing like Wintermark runes.

t.Astolat: Janon asked that Laroc Cathedral be rededicated to passion, and Tharim sought consent to destroy commissions in Dawn including the Harps of Astolat, in return for aid in the Barrens.
t.The Barrens: Imperial armies conquering the Barrens faced a one-fifth penalty unless breaking the chains of Druj slaves, while Dawn weighed mandates and eternal offers to strengthen its campaign there.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the Synod's messenger Osran recalled seeing memorial stones when his striding passed through Weirwater in his youth.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Druj armies were described as trapped in Zenith facing annihilation, prompting Dawn to see the moment to strike.

r.Astolat/The Chase: Janon offered to grant Dawnish armies triumphant charge in the Barrens if Laroc Cathedral were rededicated to passion, replacing the Dean of Laroc Cathedral with a Keeper of the Silver Flame title, ideally held by Kahendrin Wordsmith.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Dawnguard, the Dawnish stronghold destroyed by the Druj, could be guarded by Jaheris's creatures with an effective military strength of 2500 if the Empire retook it and built him a fane there.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Barren Glen regio on the edge of the Heart of Peytaht, guarded by the Druj, was the site where House Aurelius could cast Sorin's ritual to gain wolves worth 1500 strength for a season, with some remaining for eleven winters.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Mentioned in passing: Murderdale was noted as having had Dawnish settlements during centuries of contest with the Druj.

Under heaven.d: Hundreds of Imperial champions landed in Greenwall, overwhelmed Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard and burnt his hall, then raided Iron Stand, Ulfrsmoor and Eyrarfell. They sacked the Broken Chasm quarry and Ulfrshal, and looted mines, the Shining Caverns' supply lines and Steelweaver's Crucible. Thralls and ancestral sites were deliberately spared. At sea, fleets harried Jotun boats, struck Kierheim's docks and tore down defences along the Kongegőr, with the hylje's hostile 'cousins', the people of the salt, appearing in the fighting. The Jotun cannot resupply or raise armies until Spring 385YE. Greenwall is easier to capture, and the Kongegőr's damage hampers Jotun army movement. Furious northern Jarls promise an answer.

n.Dawn: Dawnish knights and yeofolk led the daring assault on the Broken Chasm quarry, which was at first repulsed before the raiders overran its defenders and looted its white granite.
n.Grendel: Half a dozen Grendel trading ships at Kierheim declared their neutrality, refused to fight alongside the Jotun and watched the battle on the docks, ready to flee.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: seven Highborn citizens are listed among the raid's participants.
n.Imperial Orcs: A warband of Imperial Orcs struck down Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard of Greenwall, and the orc Ergot was thanked for blazing the trail in the earlier raid.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost great wealth from Skallahn's mines, forges and quarries, saw Kierheim's docks raided and the Kongegőr badly damaged, and cannot resupply or raise new armies until Spring 385YE. Their northern Jarls are furious and vow an answer.
n.Navarr: Navarr raiders took part in the raid, and Navarr scouts who approached the Shining Caverns reported that its garrison had been swollen by troops from Tromsa.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: three Freeborn citizens are listed as participants, and a Freeborn corsair remarked that overladen ships were a good problem to have.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: fourteen League citizens are listed among the raid's participants.
n.The Marches: Marchers gathered at Odd's End and supplied the raid leader, Orrick of House Bolholt, and Marcher captains led attacks on the Kongegőr. The raid's success lets Steward's Landing become a permanent staging post for Marcher captains raiding the Kalsea coast.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a navigable passage through the Sea of Snow might allow a few ships to reach the coast of Otkodov, held by Thule.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: two Urizen citizens are listed among the raid's participants.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: three Varushkan citizens are listed among the raid's participants.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk gathered at Westerhal alongside hylje guides, made up a large share of the raiders and led attacks on the Kongegőr. Westerhal's fisherfolk may now fish the Gullet under Wintermark fleet escort.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: captains who berth on the Bay of Catazar crossed the Sea of Snow to the rendezvous, and the Empire's earlier scouting there is cited as a precedent.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the raid leader hoped the raid would help speed Bregasland's return to Imperial hands.
t.Hordalant: Imperial captains braved Hordalant's northern coast, and the Jarls of Hordalant joined the defence of the damaged Kongegőr. Armies crossing between Hordalant and Skallahn must now halt on arrival.
t.Kallavesa: Westerhal in Kallavesa served as a gathering and retreat point for the raid, and its fisherfolk may now bring prosperity to western Kallavesa by fishing the Gullet.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is named as one of the rendezvous points through which Imperial ships passed on the way to the raid.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: cartographers believe a passage through the Sea of Snow's ice might let a few ships reach the coast of Otkodov.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: several of the League raiders listed bear names of Sarvos.
t.Sea of Snow: Some Imperial captains pushed past the Kongegőr into the icy Sea of Snow, where the people of the salt seemed at home and cautious, unfamiliar orc warships scouted the Imperial fleets before fleeing.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the raid leader hoped to speed Sermersuaq's return to Imperial hands, and the hylje who joined the raid were dressed in the Suaq style.
t.Skallahn: Skallahn was ravaged across Greenwall, Iron Stand, Ulfrsmoor and Eyrarfell and its coast harried, leaving the Jotun unable to resupply or raise armies there until Spring 385YE. Greenwall is easier to capture, and the Jarl of Kierheim cannot move against the Imperial spy network before Winter 384YE.
t.Tromsa: The Jarl of Tromsa and his allies sent several hundred troops south to reinforce the Shining Caverns and Steelweaver's Crucible against the raiders.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Westerhal in the West Marsh launched Winterfolk vessels for the raid and offered a retreat route across the shallow straits, and may now become a thriving escorted fishing port.
r.Skallahn/Bjarkey: Bjarkey was among the coastal targets the raiding ships planned to strike as Imperial fleets harried Jotun boats and shore settlements along the Skallahn coast.
r.Skallahn/Eyrarfell: Raiders hit almost all of Eyrarfell's mines despite fierce resistance from Jarl Gilla Sverrisdóttir's ulvenwar, and looted mithril from the caravans and storehouses supplying the Shining Caverns.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: The raiders landed in Greenwall, overwhelmed Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard's warriors, burnt his hall and attacked its smithies, forges and mines. Imperial armies need one fewer victory point to capture it until Autumn 385YE.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Winterfolk warbands visited the ruins of Guntherm's Iron Banner but left the town of Overgaard untouched, while Jarl Ebbe sent warriors south to aid the defence of the Broken Chasm.
r.Skallahn/Ulfrsmoor: Raiders fought across Ulfrsmoor, sparing the temple of Ulfrskelf but storming the Broken Chasm quarry and besieging and looting Jarl Alvilda Ottesen's castle at Ulfrshal.
